We discuss how AD-related stimuli shift microglia toward a pro-inflammatory metabolic phenotype; how impaired mitochondrial quality control promotes reactive oxygen species generation and oxidized mitochondrial DNA release; and how these signals facilitate NLRP3 inflammasome activation and sustained inflammatory amplification. We further summarize therapeutic strategies targeting upstream mitochondrial homeostasis, intermediate metabolic-redox coupling, and downstream NLRP3 signaling, while emphasizing the translational limitations and biomarker needs. We conclude that this proposed axis provides a testable stage-dependent framework for interpreting chronic, self-amplifying neuroinflammation in AD and may inform biomarker-guided, combinatorial therapeutic strategies.
authors: Li S, Jin J, Liu Y, Yuan J, Dong Y, Wang Z, Li L, Zhang Y.
screening_reason: This review details microglial immunometabolic reprogramming and its role in driving NLRP3 inflammasome-mediated neuroinflammation in Alzheimer's disease.
summary_ja: 本ナラティブレビューは、アルツハイマー病（AD）におけるミクログリアの免疫代謝再プログラミングにおける、段階的な「ミトコンドリア機能障害-活性酸素種の不均衡-NLRP3インフラマソーム」軸を提唱している。AD関連の刺激がミクログリアを炎症性代謝表現型へとシフトさせ、ミトコンドリアの品質管理不全が活性酸素種の生成や酸化ミトコンドリアDNAの放出を促してNLRP3インフラマソームを活性化する機序を解説している。さらに、この軸を標的とした治療戦略をまとめ、トランスレーショナルな課題やバイオマーカーの必要性について議論している。
summary_en: This narrative review proposes a stage-dependent mitochondrial dysfunction-redox imbalance-NLRP3 inflammasome axis in microglial immunometabolic reprogramming during Alzheimer's disease (AD). It discusses how AD-related stimuli shift microglia toward a pro-inflammatory metabolic phenotype and how impaired mitochondrial quality control promotes reactive oxygen species and oxidized DNA release to activate the NLRP3 inflammasome. The review also summarizes therapeutic strategies targeting this axis and highlights translational limitations and biomarker needs.
key_finding_ja: アルツハイマー病における持続的な神経炎症の機序として、ミトコンドリア機能障害、酸化ストレスの不均衡、およびNLRP3インフラマソーム活性化が連動する段階的な軸を提唱した。
why_it_matters_ja: この提唱された軸は、アルツハイマー病における慢性的な神経炎症を理解するための検証可能な枠組みを提供し、将来的なバイオマーカー主導の複合治療戦略の開発に寄与する可能性がある。

title: Microalgae Hybrid Biosystem for Enhanced Oral Delivery of Rifaximin in Hepatic Encephalopathy Treatment.
abstract: Hepatic encephalopathy (HE) is a serious neuropsychiatric complication of acute or chronic liver failure. It occurred in approximately 40% of acute liver failure cases and affected 30%-45% of patients with chronic liver failure or decompensated cirrhosis. Hyperammonemia is widely recognized as a central pathogenic factor in the pathogenesis of HE. Rifaximin (RIF), a non-absorbable oral antibiotic, was widely used to manage HE by modulating gut microbiota and reducing ammonia production. However, its clinical efficacy remained suboptimal due to poor aqueous solubility, limited dispersibility, and inadequate gastrointestinal retention. These limitations were further exacerbated in severe cases, owing to restricted oral dosing, recurrence associated with poor adherence, and potential risks of antimicrobial resistance and infection-related adverse events. This study presented a microalgae-nanoparticle hybrid system (SP@RIF) for drug delivery, in which RIF-encapsulated nanoparticles (RIFnano) were electrostatically loaded onto the surface of Spirulina platensis (SP), aiming to improve the oral delivery and therapeutic efficiency in HE treatment. RIFnano exhibited significantly enhanced antibacterial activity compared to free RIF. SP@RIF demonstrated prolonged gastrointestinal retention and sustained drug release profiles. In mouse models of HE, oral administration of SP@RIF markedly reduced systemic ammonia levels and improved behavioral outcomes. Furthermore, SP@RIF enhanced intestinal barrier function, attenuated systemic inflammation and neuroinflammation, ameliorated cognitive impairments, and modulated the gut microbiota. Importantly, these therapeutic benefits were achieved without observable toxicity. These findings highlight SP@RIF as a potential therapeutic strategy for treating HE.
authors: Wang K, Huang X, Yang L, Liu J, Lei L, Zou S, Wang K, Zhou M, Tang Z.
screening_reason: The study evaluates a drug delivery system that attenuates neuroinflammation and modulates the gut microbiota in a model of hepatic encephalopathy.
summary_ja: 本研究は、肝性脳症（HE）の治療においてリファキシミンの経口投与効率を向上させるため、微細藻類とナノ粒子のハイブリッドドラッグデリバリーシステム（SP@RIF）を開発した。SP@RIFは、遊離リファキシミンと比較して優れた抗菌活性を示し、胃腸内での滞留時間を延長させ、持続的な薬物放出を実現した。肝性脳症のマウスモデルにおいて、SP@RIFの経口投与は毒性を示すことなく、血中アンモニア濃度を有意に低下させ、神経炎症を緩和し、認知機能を改善するとともに腸内細菌叢を調整した。
summary_en: This study developed a microalgae-nanoparticle hybrid drug delivery system (SP@RIF) to enhance the oral delivery of rifaximin for treating hepatic encephalopathy (HE). SP@RIF demonstrated prolonged gastrointestinal retention, sustained drug release, and enhanced antibacterial activity compared to free rifaximin. In HE mouse models, oral administration of SP@RIF significantly reduced blood ammonia levels, attenuated neuroinflammation, improved cognitive function, and modulated the gut microbiota without observable toxicity.
key_finding_ja: 微細藻類スピルリナを用いたハイブリッドナノシステムSP@RIFは、リファキシミンの経口送達効率を劇的に向上させ、肝性脳症モデルマウスのアンモニア血症や神経炎症を効果的に改善した。
why_it_matters_ja: 溶解性や体内滞留性の低さというリファキシミンの課題を克服する新たな送達技術として、肝性脳症のより効果的かつ安全な治療法の開発に寄与することが期待される。

title: Integrating gut‑brain axis insights into bundled nutrition care for critically ill patients: From mechanisms to implementation (Review).
abstract: Critical illness induces a marked disruption of the gut‑brain axis, which is characterized by systemic inflammation and the rapid collapse of intestinal barrier integrity. These pathological shifts facilitate the translocation of pathogen‑associated molecular patterns, thereby driving neuroinflammation and exacerbating intensive care unit‑acquired syndromes such as delirium and muscular wasting. Although conventional nutritional strategies emphasize caloric and protein goals, emerging evidence has highlighted the necessity of modulating the host‑microbiome interface to preserve neurological and systemic homeostasis. The integration of fermentable fibers, probiotics and specialized lipid mediators into a standardized framework may effectively interrupt the self‑perpetuating cycle of dysbiosis and organ failure. The present review uniquely contributes to the field by integrating an implementation science framework for clinical bundle application and discussing artificial intelligence driven precision nutrition advances, which are topics that have not been comprehensively covered in the majority of previous reviews. Therefore, the present review bridges mechanistic insights with practical, scalable strategies to optimize nutritional care and improve recovery trajectories in patients with critical illness.
authors: Zhang L, Yang S, Wu H, Zhou H.
screening_reason: This review focuses on gut-brain axis disruption, gut microbiome modulation, and neuroinflammation in critically ill patients.
summary_ja: 本総説は、重症疾患時における腸脳相関の破綻が、全身性炎症、腸管バリア機能の崩壊、そして神経炎症を引き起こすメカニズムについて議論している。発酵性食物繊維、プロバイオティクス、特殊な脂質メディエーターを用いて宿主とマイクロバイオームの相互作用を調整することが、恒常性の維持に有効である可能性を強調している。さらに、臨床現場への導入を容易にする実装科学の枠組みや、人工知能（AI）を活用した精密栄養学の進歩についても統合的に解説している。
summary_en: This review discusses the disruption of the gut-brain axis during critical illness, which leads to systemic inflammation, intestinal barrier collapse, and neuroinflammation. It highlights the potential of modulating the host-microbiome interface using fermentable fibers, probiotics, and specialized lipid mediators to preserve homeostasis. Additionally, the review integrates implementation science and AI-driven precision nutrition to provide practical, scalable strategies for clinical care.
key_finding_ja: 重症患者における腸脳相関の破綻を防ぐため、マイクロバイオームを標的とした栄養介入とAI駆動型精密栄養学や実装科学を統合したケアパッケージの重要性が提示された。
why_it_matters_ja: 従来のカロリー管理にとどまらず、腸内細菌叢を考慮した多角的な栄養管理を標準化することで、重症患者の全身状態や認知機能の回復を促進できる可能性がある。

title: IL-17A levels in Alzheimer's disease brains are mediated by X chromosome dosage.
abstract: Among inflammatory mediators, interleukin-17A (IL-17A) has emerged as a potential contributor to AD pathogenesis, although its role remains incompletely defined. Notably, sex differences are evident in AD, with males exhibiting earlier mortality and greater cognitive deficits during aging and preclinical stages compared to females. While hormonal influences have been widely studied, the contribution of sex chromosome complement was suggested critical and remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated the impact of sex chromosome on cognitive function and neuroinflammation using amyloid and tau mouse models. Female Tg2576 and PS19 mice were crossed with XY* males to generate XX, XO, XY, and XXY genotypes, enabling separation of X from Y chromosomal effect. Behavioral assessments, including fear conditioning, novel object recognition, and Barnes maze, revealed that XY mice exhibited significantly greater cognitive impairment compared to XX and XXY counterparts. The same pattern was seen in IL-17A levels, indicating an effect of X chromosome instead of Y. Amyloid-β and phosphorylated tau pathology by immunohistochemistry and Elisa confirmed robust disease-associated accumulation in Tg2576 and PS19 mice, but showed no differences across sex chromosome complements. Collectively, our study identifies X chromosome dosage as a key modulator of cognitive resilience and IL-17A-linked neuroinflammation in AD models. Future studies focused on understanding how X-linked factors regulate IL17 mediated neuroinflammatory pathways could reveal novel therapeutic targets for AD.
authors: Misrani A, Wang J, Xu Y, Liu F.
screening_reason: The study investigates the impact of sex chromosome dosage on IL-17A-linked neuroinflammation in Alzheimer's disease models.
summary_ja: 本研究は、アルツハイマー病（AD）のマウスモデルを用いて、性染色体の構成が認知機能および神経炎症に与える影響を調査した。XX、XO、XY、XXYの異なる遺伝子型を作製して比較した結果、XYマウスはXXおよびXXYマウスと比較して、認知機能障害が有意に強く、IL-17Aレベルも高いことが示された。この違いはY染色体ではなくX染色体の数（コピー数）に起因しており、アミロイドβやリン酸化タウの蓄積量には差が見られなかった。
summary_en: This study examined the impact of sex chromosome complement on cognitive function and neuroinflammation in mouse models of Alzheimer's disease (AD). By generating various sex chromosome genotypes (XX, XO, XY, XXY), the researchers demonstrated that XY mice exhibited greater cognitive impairment and higher IL-17A levels compared to XX and XXY mice. These differences were mediated by X chromosome dosage rather than Y chromosome effects, while amyloid-β and tau pathologies remained unaffected.
key_finding_ja: アルツハイマー病モデルにおいて、X染色体のコピー数が認知機能の維持およびIL-17Aを介した神経炎症の抑制に重要な役割を果たしていることが明らかになった。
why_it_matters_ja: 性染色体によるAD病態の修飾機構が解明されることで、性差を考慮した個別化医療や、IL-17Aを標的とした新たな治療法の開発につながる可能性がある。

title: Hexokinase-3 upregulation and histone H3K18 lactylation mediate murine liver fibrosis induced by Echinococcus multilocularis.
abstract: Alveolar echinococcosis (AE), caused by Echinococcus multilocularis infection, leads to destructive hepatic lesions and severe hepatic fibrosis. Lactylation, a post-translational modification, has been linked to fibrotic progression in hepatocytes. However, the role of E. multilocularis infection in hepatic lactylation remains unclear. This study aims to elucidate the relationship between hepatic fibrosis and lactylation induced by E. multilocularis infection and fill this knowledge gap. The results showed that lactate concentrations in the livers and sera of AE mice were significantly elevated compared with those in the control group. The relative mRNA expression of hexokinase isoforms in the liver tissue of AE mouse models revealed significant upregulation of hexokinase-3 (HK3), a key enzyme regulating lactate production. Immunofluorescence staining revealed substantial colocalization between HK3 and TGF-β1 in hepatic lesions of AE mice. Western blot analysis using a pan-lactylation antibody showed significantly elevated lactylation levels in the livers of AE mice compared with controls, with a significant increase in histone H3 lysine 18 lactylation (H3K18la). CUT&Tag analysis revealed differential enrichment of H3K18la at multiple fibrosis-associated genes in AE mouse liver. In vitro, AML-12 hepatocytes exposed to E. multilocularis culture supernatant showed significant upregulation of TGF-β1, HK3, and histone lactylation. HK3 knockdown significantly reduced the induction of H3K18la and fibrosis-related proteins, whereas exogenous lactate supplementation significantly increased these responses despite HK3 silencing, confirming that lactate acts downstream of HK3 to drive histone lactylation and fibrogenesis. Corosolic acid, a compound that limits HK3-mediated lactate production, attenuated histone lactylation and fibrosis-related protein expression. These findings indicate that HK3-driven histone lactylation at H3K18 contributes to hepatic fibrosis in AE, and suggest that HK3 may serve as promising therapeutic targets for AE.
authors: Miao Y, Shan L, Liu J, Cui W, Yang X, Xiu L, Yang W, Li C, Liu W, Wang Y, Zhang T, Hu W.
screening_reason: The study investigates the role of histone H3K18 lactylation, a post-translational modification, in driving hepatic fibrosis.
summary_ja: 本研究は、多包条虫（Echinococcus multilocularis）感染によって引き起こされる肝線維化における肝臓の乳酸修飾（ラクチル化）の役割を調査した。感染マウスの肝臓では乳酸濃度が上昇し、乳酸産生を制御するヘキソキナーゼ3（HK3）の発現が有意に上昇していることが示された。このHK3の上昇は、線維化関連遺伝子におけるヒストンH3リシン18のラクチル化（H3K18la）を促進し、線維化を進行させることが明らかになった。HK3のノックダウンやコロソリン酸による治療は、このヒストンラクチル化と線維化関連タンパク質の発現を抑制した。
summary_en: This study investigated the role of hepatic lactylation in liver fibrosis induced by Echinococcus multilocularis infection. The researchers found that infection significantly elevated lactate levels and upregulated hexokinase-3 (HK3) in mouse livers. This HK3 upregulation promoted histone H3 lysine 18 lactylation (H3K18la) at fibrosis-associated genes, driving fibrogenesis. Knockdown of HK3 or treatment with corosolic acid attenuated this lactylation and reduced the expression of fibrosis-related proteins.
key_finding_ja: 多包条虫感染による肝線維化において、HK3の上昇に伴うヒストンH3K18のラクチル化が線維化関連遺伝子の発現を促進し、病態を増悪させることが明らかになった。
why_it_matters_ja: 本研究の成果は、多包条虫症による重篤な肝線維化に対する新たな治療標的としてHK3やヒストンラクチル化経路が有望である可能性を示唆している。

title: Early-life immune imprinting by a B. infantis-HMO synbiotic shapes infant immune signatures and protects against experimental respiratory disease.
abstract: Early microbial colonization influences immune development, with lower abundance of human milk oligosaccharide (HMO)-utilizing bifidobacteria linked to immune-related disorder risk. Here, we demonstrate that synbiotic supplementation with Bifidobacterium infantis (LMG 11588) and a blend of six structurally diverse HMOs plus Bifidobacterium lactis (CNCM I-3446) altered gut microbiome composition, changed systemic immune cell-networks, and reduced persistence of a T helper 2 (Th2) bias in formula-fed infants, following a pattern observed in breastfed infants. In preclinical models, synbiotic reduces lower respiratory tract infection (LRI) severity and aberrant type-2 immune responses and confers lasting immune benefits into adulthood. These effects are associated with changes in the circulating metabolome, including increased 12(S)-hydroxyheptadecatrienoic acid (12-HHT), which correlates with improved infection outcomes and phenocopies synbiotic-mediated protection when administered orally. Together, these findings indicate that infant-type synbiotic supplementation during a critical early-life window can imprint immune function and promote disease tolerance.
authors: Rashid RB, Chung CK, Namubiru P, Ahmed T, CLARA Study Group, Howard DR, Sebina I, Wilkins T, Rana MS, Morrow JP, Creek DJ, Moll JM, Vidal K, Fumero C, Lavalle L, Maes D, Hays NP, Silva-Zolezzi I, Forbes-Blom E, Sprenger N, Picaud JC, Phipps S, Noti M.
screening_reason: The paper investigates how synbiotic supplementation alters gut microbiome composition and shapes infant immune development.
summary_ja: 乳児期早期の微生物定着が免疫発達に与える影響を調べるため、Bifidobacterium infantisとヒトミルクオリゴ糖（HMO）などを組み合わせたシンバイオティクスの効果を検証した。このシンバイオティクス摂取は、人工乳栄養児の腸内細菌叢を変化させ、全身の免疫細胞ネットワークを調整し、Th2バイアスを抑制した。さらに前臨床モデルにおいて、呼吸器感染症の重症度を低下させ、その保護効果は代謝物12-HHTの上昇と関連して成人期まで持続した。
summary_en: This study demonstrated that early-life supplementation with a B. infantis and HMO-based synbiotic altered gut microbiome composition and systemic immune networks in formula-fed infants. In preclinical models, the synbiotic reduced the severity of lower respiratory tract infections and conferred long-lasting immune benefits into adulthood. These protective effects were associated with changes in the circulating metabolome, specifically an increase in 12-HHT.
key_finding_ja: B. infantisとHMOを含むシンバイオティクスは、乳児の腸内細菌叢と免疫ネットワークを調整し、呼吸器感染症に対する長期的な保護効果をもたらす。
why_it_matters_ja: 乳児期早期の適切な介入が、生涯にわたる免疫機能の形成や呼吸器疾患への抵抗力を高めるための新たな予防戦略となる可能性がある。

title: Characterization of Post-translational Modification in Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatohepatitis: Acetylation, Lactylation, and Phosphorylation.
abstract: In metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), abnormalities in post-translational modification (PTM) are both a consequence of the pathological process and a driving force for disease progression. Therefore, this study intends to characterize the PTM features (acetylation, lactylation, and phosphorylation) of MASH, which will provide a crucial theoretical basis for the diagnosis and development of new targets for MASH. In this study, protein/modification profiles of clinical liver tissues from Normal and MASH were analyzed by LC-MS to identify differentially expressed proteins (DEPs) and differentially modified proteins (DMPs) with acetylation, lactylation, and phosphorylation. This study found that acetylation and lactylation occurred mainly in K, whose upstream and downstream amino acids consisted of A, G, K, R, and V. Phosphorylation occurred mainly in S and T, whose upstream and downstream ones consisted of D, E, P, R, and S. Proteomics with ordinary, acetylation, lactylation, and phosphorylation identified 468, 433, 434, and 1,471 DEPs/DMPs, respectively, which mainly regulate cytoskeleton, immunity, proliferation, oxidative stress, inflammatory cascades, various metabolisms (sugars, amino acids, lipids, and carbon). CMKLR1, CYP2E1, GLRX, and XRCC1 were identified as key regulators in the shared DEPs of ordinary proteomics and modification proteomics. Notably, the differences in expression of the four proteins in clinical liver tissues from Normal and MASH were consistent with the proteomics results. In conclusion, this study systematically reveals the global dysregulation of PTM, emphasizing CMKLR1, CYP2E1, GLRX, and XRCC1 as the key proteins/modification sites, and provides new perspectives for targeted intervention in MASH.
authors: Li K, Li Y, Zhang Y, Song S, Pa C, Du C, Yang L, Xue G, Gao H.
screening_reason: This study characterizes protein post-translational modifications (acetylation, lactylation, and phosphorylation) in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH).
summary_ja: 代謝機能障害関連脂肪肝炎（MASH）における翻訳後修飾（PTM）の特徴を明らかにするため、臨床肝組織のプロテオーム解析を実施した。アセチル化、ラクチル化、およびリン酸化のプロファイルをLC-MSを用いて分析し、変動タンパク質および変動修飾タンパク質を同定した。これらの修飾は細胞骨格、免疫、増殖、酸化ストレス、炎症、代謝経路の制御に関与しており、CMKLR1、CYP2E1、GLRX、XRCC1が重要な制御因子として同定された。
summary_en: This study characterized the post-translational modification (PTM) profiles, including acetylation, lactylation, and phosphorylation, in clinical liver tissues from patients with MASH. Quantitative proteomics identified numerous differentially modified proteins involved in cytoskeleton regulation, immunity, oxidative stress, and metabolism. CMKLR1, CYP2E1, GLRX, and XRCC1 were highlighted as key regulatory proteins associated with these modifications.
key_finding_ja: MASH患者の肝組織においてアセチル化、ラクチル化、リン酸化の網羅的プロファイルを明らかにし、病態に関与する重要な制御因子としてCMKLR1、CYP2E1、GLRX、XRCC1を同定した。
why_it_matters_ja: MASHの病態生理における翻訳後修飾の役割が解明されたことで、新たな診断マーカーや治療標的の開発につながる可能性がある。

title: An innovative organoid model to screen for bacteria and their metabolites that protect against inflammation-induced colonic barrier disruption.
abstract: Organoids provide a useful model system to study interactions between gut microbes and the activity of host tissues, including gastrointestinal (GI) barrier function. However, most organoid models have limited capacity to mimic the physiological hypoxia experienced by the colonic epithelium in vivo . While oxygen is required to support respiration in the host cells, many gut microbes are anaerobes that require anoxic conditions to grow. Using an innovative anaerobe co-culture system that maintains constant oxygen concentrations on the basolateral side of colonic epithelial monolayers and anoxic conditions on the luminal side, we demonstrate that colonic monolayers derived from a primary human cell line behaved more like in vivo epithelia when cultivated in the co-culture system than when cultured under ambient oxygen concentrations. We then identified interactions between the colonic epithelium and a strain of Bifidobacterium adolescentis -an oxygen-sensitive species that is prevalent and abundant in the adult gut microbiome. Co-culturing colonic monolayers with Bifidobacterium adolescentis U269-1 in the anoxic apical chamber mitigated loss of the barrier function in monolayers exposed to inflammatory cytokines. We identified indole lactic acid (ILA) as one metabolite from B. adolescentis that provides dose-dependent protection against inflammatory cytokines. Oral administration of ILA was well tolerated in mice and provided protection against immunotherapy-induced (anti-CTLA4) colitis in female, but not male mice. Together, we demonstrated the utility of the co-culture system for screening microbes and their metabolites for interactions with the colonic epithelium, as well as advancing our understanding of interactions between bifidobacteria and host barrier function. IMPORTANCE The present study yielded strong evidence for the beneficial effects of B. adolescentis on the maintenance of colonic barrier function in an asymmetric oxygen system that mimics the colonic environment. The bifidobacterial metabolite indole lactic acid was implicated in this protection both in vitro and in a mouse model. We also refined and scaled the co-culture system to a 96-well plate format to provide the capacity for higher-throughput screening of microbes and microbial metabolites under physiologically relevant conditions.
authors: Cady N, Meyer SR, Kim K, Lo BC, So N, Chen GY, Rosshart SP, Shah YM, Núñez G, Sexton JZ, Schmidt TM.
screening_reason: The paper centers on gut bacteria (Bifidobacterium adolescentis) and microbial metabolite interactions with the colonic epithelium to protect intestinal barrier function.
summary_ja: 著者らは、大腸上皮細胞の基底側に酸素を供給しつつ腔側を無酸素状態に保つ非対称的共培養システムを開発し、生理的条件に近いヒト大腸オルガノイド単層モデルを構築した。このモデルを用いて嫌気性菌であるBifidobacterium adolescentis U269-1を評価したところ、炎症性サイトカインによる上皮バリア機能障害が軽減されることが見出された。さらに、同菌が産生する代謝物インドール乳酸（ILA）が用量依存的にバリア保護作用を発揮することを確認した。マウスモデルにおいても、ILAの経口投与が抗CTLA4抗体誘発性大腸炎に対して軽減効果を示すことが確認された。
summary_en: Researchers developed an asymmetric oxygen co-culture system that maintains apical anoxia and basolateral oxygenation, enabling physiologically relevant modeling of human colonic epithelial monolayers. Using this platform, Bifidobacterium adolescentis U269-1 and its metabolite indole lactic acid (ILA) were shown to protect against cytokine-induced epithelial barrier disruption. Furthermore, oral ILA administration mitigated immunotherapy-induced colitis in a mouse model.
key_finding_ja: 生理的低酸素を再現した器官共培養系により、Bifidobacterium adolescentis由来代謝物インドール乳酸が炎症性大腸バリア障害を軽減することが示された。
why_it_matters_ja: 生体内環境を模倣した評価プラットフォームは、腸内細菌やその代謝産物を利用した新規バリア保護療法のスクリーニングに役立つ可能性がある。

title: System x c - deficiency suppresses microglial glutamate release and inflammation, ameliorating motor dysfunction and anxiety-like behaviors in aged mice.
abstract: Elevated extracellular glutamate and neuroinflammation are well-established contributors to aging-related phenotypes. However, the cellular sources of extracellular glutamate and the underlying molecular mechanisms remain poorly understood. Therefore, this study aimed to determine the role of microglial system x c - , as a candidate source of extracellular glutamate, in physiological brain aging. Using aged xCT knockout (xCTKO) mice, which lack the functional subunit of system x c - , primary microglia, and cultured microglial cells, we examined xCT expression, glutamate release, inflammatory responses, oxidative status, and aging-related behavioral phenotypes. Here, we demonstrate that the microglial system x c - is a major source of pathological extracellular glutamate in the aging mouse brain. Physiological aging, as well as aging-related stimuli significantly increased xCT expression in microglia. Genetic deletion or pharmacological inhibition of xCT significantly attenuated microglial glutamate release, which was enhanced by age-related xCT upregulation. Notably, although TNF-α protein expression was reduced in the brain of aged xCTKO mice compared with that of aged wild-type mice, TNF-α mRNA levels remained elevated. The reduction in TNF-α protein expression was rescued by N-acetyl-l-cysteine, an xCT-independent source of cysteine, suggesting that xCT deficiency suppresses inflammatory cytokine synthesis through reduced intracellular cysteine availability. Furthermore, aged xCTKO mice exhibited improved motor function and reduced anxiety-like behavior without exacerbating oxidative stress or affecting neuronal number. Collectively, these findings identify microglial xCT as an important source of extracellular glutamate during physiological aging and demonstrate that xCT deficiency suppresses microglial glutamate release and neuroinflammation, thereby ameliorating aging-related phenotypes.
authors: Kato Y, Takemoto T, Yabe M, Kanatani M, Sato H, Iwata M, Horikoshi Y, Nakaso K.
screening_reason: The study directly investigates how microglial system x c - deficiency suppresses microglial glutamate release and neuroinflammation in the aging brain.
summary_ja: 本研究は、生理的老化脳におけるマイクログリアのシスチン/グルタミン酸交換輸送体（システムx c -、xCT）の役割と神経炎症への影響を調査しました。加齢に伴いマイクログリアでxCTの発現が上昇し、これが病的な細胞外グルタミン酸の主要な供給源となることが示されました。xCTの遺伝子欠損または薬理学的阻害は、マイクログリアからのグルタミン酸放出を抑制し、細胞内システインの利用能を低下させることで炎症性サイトカイン（TNF-α）の産生を抑え、老齢マウスの運動機能低下や不安様行動を改善しました。
summary_en: This study investigates the role of microglial system x c - (xCT) in physiological brain aging and neuroinflammation. The authors found that xCT expression is upregulated in microglia during aging, serving as a major source of pathological extracellular glutamate. Genetic deletion or pharmacological inhibition of xCT reduced microglial glutamate release and suppressed TNF-α protein synthesis by limiting intracellular cysteine availability, which ultimately ameliorated motor dysfunction and anxiety-like behaviors in aged mice.
key_finding_ja: 加齢に伴い上昇するマイクログリアのxCTが病的な細胞外グルタミン酸の放出源であり、その欠損が神経炎症を抑制して老齢マウスの運動機能や不安様行動を改善することが明らかになった。
why_it_matters_ja: 加齢に伴う認知・運動機能低下や精神症状に対して、マイクログリアのxCTを標的とした新たな治療アプローチが有効である可能性を示唆しています。

title: Mutating different α-tubulin acetylation sites has distinct effects on axon terminal morphogenesis in Drosophila melanogaster .
abstract: Microtubules are created from uniform α- and β-tubulin building blocks but typically carry out a variety of specialized functions within a cell. The post-translational modification of tubulin is one means by which microtubule function can be tuned to match different cellular activities. While multiple sites of acetylation have been identified in tubulin, particularly α-tubulin, the effect(s) of acetylation at different sites on microtubule function remain poorly characterized. Here, we took a genetic approach in Drosophila to disrupt three conserved sites of acetylation (K326, K370, and K401) in endogenous α-tubulin and characterized the effects on neuronal development. Acetylation-blocking mutagenesis of α-tubulin K326 (K326A) perturbed larval locomotion and reduced stable microtubules, suggesting that the α-tubulin K326A mutation exerts its effect by disrupting microtubule stability. In contrast, mutagenesis of α-tubulin K370 and K401 had virtually no effect on microtubule stability, suggesting that the effects of these mutations on axon terminal morphogenesis and survival may be mediated through a different mechanism. Altogether, the varied effects of these mutations suggest that acetylation at these three different sites may regulate different aspects of microtubule function within developing neurons.
authors: Than H, Welch CJ, Schauer E, Trujillo SP, Wildonger J.
screening_reason: The study investigates the effects of mutating specific tubulin acetylation sites, focusing on the role of this post-translational modification in neuronal development.
summary_ja: 本研究は、ショウジョウバエを用いて、内因性α-チューブリンの3つの保存されたアセチル化部位（K326、K370、K401）の変異が神経発達に及ぼす影響を遺伝学的に解析した。K326のアセチル化を阻害する変異は、幼虫の運動能力を低下させ、安定な微小管を減少させることが明らかになった。一方で、K370およびK401の変異は微小管の安定性には影響を与えなかったが、異なる機序を介して軸索末端の形態形成や生存に影響を及ぼした。これらの結果は、異なる部位のアセチル化が、発達中のニューロンにおいて微小管機能の異なる側面を制御している可能性を示唆している。
summary_en: This study investigated the effects of mutating three conserved acetylation sites (K326, K370, and K401) in endogenous α-tubulin on neuronal development in Drosophila. Mutagenesis of K326 perturbed larval locomotion and reduced microtubule stability, whereas mutations at K370 and K401 affected axon terminal morphogenesis and survival without altering microtubule stability. These findings suggest that acetylation at different sites regulates distinct aspects of microtubule function in developing neurons.
key_finding_ja: α-チューブリンの異なるアセチル化部位（K326、K370、K401）の変異は、微小管の安定性や軸索末端の形態形成に対してそれぞれ異なる影響を及ぼす。
why_it_matters_ja: チューブリンの翻訳後修飾が神経発達において果たす多様な役割の理解を深め、微小管機能を標的とした神経疾患研究に新たな知見をもたらす可能性がある。

title: Aurantio-Obtusin Attenuates Aβ-Induced Cognitive Impairment and Synaptic Dysfunction by Suppressing Neuroinflammation in Mice.
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) features Aβ-driven neuroinflammation and synaptic dysfunction that converge on cognitive decline, underscoring the potential value of multi-target interventions. Aurantio-obtusin (AO), a bioactive anthraquinone from Cassia obtusifolia L., exhibits reported anti-inflammatory and antioxidant activities; however, whether AO counteracts Aβ-associated behavioral impairment through coordinated modulation of inflammatory and synaptic alterations remains unclear. Here, we investigated whether AO alleviates Aβ₁₋₄₂-induced cognitive deficits and examined synapse- and inflammation-related molecular correlates. Male C57BL/6 mice received intracerebroventricular Aβ₁₋₄₂ to establish an acute AD-like model and were treated with AO (10 mg/kg/day, oral gavage) for consecutive weeks. The results showed that AO improved spatial learning and memory in the Morris water maze, recognition memory in the novel object recognition test, and working memory in the Y-maze, without affecting spontaneous locomotor activity. Furthermore, AO alleviated synaptic dysfunction by restoring synaptophysin expression and upregulating GAD65, and mitigated neuroinflammation by elevating anti-inflammatory factors (IL-4, IL-10, ARG1) and reducing TNF-α. In vitro experiments confirmed that AO was non-cytotoxic to N2A APP cells across 0-80 μM, mildly downregulated BACE1 expression, and suppressed the Aβ-induced upregulation of pro-inflammatory mediators (IL-6, iNOS) in BV2 microglial cells. Overall, AO attenuated Aβ 1-42 -driven behavioral impairment in parallel with improvements in synapse-associated markers and inflammatory readouts. These findings support further evaluation of AO as a natural compound associated with modulation of Aβ-related neuroinflammatory and synapse-associated alterations.
authors: Feng X, Yu W, Guo S, Ji Y, Li J, Wang L, Zhong G, Li S, Niu L, Zhu D, Zhou K, Du Y.
journal: Journal of neuroimmune pharmacology : the official journal of the Society on NeuroImmune Pharmacology
screening_reason: The principal finding demonstrates that Aurantio-Obtusin attenuates cognitive impairment by directly suppressing neuroinflammation and microglial inflammatory mediators.
summary_ja: エビスグサ種子由来の化合物オウランティオオプチシン（AO）が、アミロイドベータ（Aβ1-42）誘発性の認知機能障害および神経炎症に与える影響をマウスモデルで検証した。AOの投与により、水迷路試験や新規物体認知試験における学習・記憶障害が改善し、自発運動量に影響を与えることなく作業記憶も回復した。さらにAOはシナプトフィジンの発現回復や抗炎症性因子の増加、TNF-αの低下をもたらした。インビトロ実験においても、AOはミクログリアにおける炎症性メディエーターの発現を抑制することが確認された。
summary_en: This study evaluated the protective effects of aurantio-obtusin (AO) against Aβ1-42-induced cognitive deficits and neuroinflammation in a mouse model. Treatment with AO restored spatial and working memory while improving synapse-associated markers and increasing anti-inflammatory cytokines. In vitro experiments further demonstrated that AO suppressed Aβ-induced pro-inflammatory mediators in microglial cells.
key_finding_ja: オウランティオオプチシンは、Aβ投与マウスにおいて神経炎症を抑えシナプス機能を回復させることで認知機能障害を改善した。
why_it_matters_ja: アミロイドベータによる神経炎症とシナプス機能障害を同時に標的とする天然化合物の新たな治療候補として期待されるが、今後の詳細な作用機序解明が求められる。

title: PALM-Scan enables single-molecule site-specific detection of protein S-palmitoylation with a nanopore.
abstract: Protein S-palmitoylation is a dynamic and reversible post-translational modification (PTM) that governs diverse cellular processes, yet its study remains constrained by the indirect and ensemble-averaging nature of classical biochemical assays. Here, we report a nanopore-based platform, PALM-Scan (palmitoylation analysis via label-free monitoring and signature capture on nanopore) that directly transduces physicochemical signatures of S-palmitoylated peptides into digital electrical signals. Using an engineered Mycobacterium smegmatis porin A (M2-MspA) nanopore, PALM-Scan enables sequence-independent identification of S-palmitoylation and simultaneously differentiates S-palmitoylation from other cysteine-directed PTMs, including S-nitrosylation and S-glutathionylation, without probes or enrichment. We further demonstrate its translational potential by successfully detecting and distinguishing S-palmitoylated subpopulations of disease-relevant biomarkers, including mouse beclin-1 (BECN1)- and glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP)-derived peptides, in complex mixtures with minimal sample input. In summary, by integrating label-free operation, single-molecule resolution, and multiplex discrimination, PALM-Scan provides a transformative tool for interrogating S-palmitoylation dynamics in both basic research and biomedical applications.
authors: Zhang Z, Yang X, Sun Y, Hao Y, Li Y, Wang Y, Xie C, Peng P, Liu S, Jiang X, Zhang Z, Kong E, Wang L, Yang A.
screening_reason: Develops a single-molecule nanopore platform directly measuring site-specific protein S-palmitoylation, a key post-translational modification.
summary_ja: タンパク質のS-パルミトイル化を直接かつ単一分子レベルで検出するナノポア技術「PALM-Scan」が開発された。改変型MspAナノポアを用いることで、標識や濃縮工程を必要とせずにS-パルミトイル化ペプチドの物理化学的特徴を電気信号へと変換することに成功した。また、S-ニトロシル化やS-グルタチオン化など他のシステイン修飾との識別や配列に依存しない同定が可能であった。BECN1やGFAP由来ペプチドを用いた実証実験により、複雑な混合物中での病的バイオマーカーのサブグループ検出における有用性が示された。
summary_en: The authors developed PALM-Scan, a nanopore-based platform for direct, label-free, single-molecule detection of protein S-palmitoylation. Utilizing an engineered MspA nanopore, the technique discriminates S-palmitoylation from other cysteine PTMs without probes or enrichment steps. Its translational capacity was demonstrated by distinguishing S-palmitoylated subpopulations of disease-relevant peptides, including BECN1 and GFAP.
key_finding_ja: ナノポア技術を用いたPALM-Scanにより、ラベルフリーかつ単一分子解像度でタンパク質のS-パルミトイル化を他のシステイン修飾と区別して検出することに成功した。
why_it_matters_ja: 様々な疾患に関連するタンパク質修飾の動態を簡便かつ高精度に解析する新たな計測基盤となることが期待される。

title: Interleukin-25: orchestrating resistance to intestinal helminth infections.
abstract: Interleukin-25 (IL-25) has emerged as a central regulator of type 2 immunity at mucosal surfaces. Beyond its classical role as an epithelial alarmin, IL-25 acts as a multifunctional coordinator of epithelial sensing, immune activation, and tissue adaptation during helminth infection. In the intestine, tuft cells detect helminth- and microbiota-derived metabolites and activate a feed-forward circuit with type 2 innate lymphoid cells (ILC2s), promoting antiparasitic immunity and barrier protection. Emerging evidence further links IL-25 to neuroimmune communication, epithelial remodeling, tissue resilience, and disease tolerance. Here, we summarize recent advances in IL-25 biology, including ILC2 specialization and the distinct roles of IL-25 in nematode and trematode infections, highlighting its potential as a therapeutic target to enhance mucosal protection while limiting immunopathology.
authors: Cociancic P, Fiallos E, Esteban JG, Muñoz-Antoli C, Toledo R.
screening_reason: Focuses on IL-25 driven intestinal mucosal immunity, epithelial metabolite sensing, and neuroimmune communication.
summary_ja: インターロイキン-25（IL-25）は粘膜表面における2型免疫の主要な調節因子として機能している。腸管においてはタフト細胞が寄生虫や腸内細菌由来の代謝物を感知し、2型自然リンパ球（ILC2）とのフィードフォワード回路を活性化して駆虫免疫やバリア保護を推進する。近年の研究により、IL-25は神経免疫連関や上皮のリモデリング、組織のレジリエンス維持にも関与することが明らかになりつつある。本総説では、線虫や吸虫感染におけるIL-25の役割やILC2の専門化に関する最新の知見をまとめている。
summary_en: This review highlights the central role of interleukin-25 in orchestrating type 2 immunity and tissue adaptation during intestinal helminth infections. In the intestine, tuft cells detect microbial and helminth metabolites to activate ILC2-mediated antiparasitic responses and barrier protection. Recent findings also connect IL-25 to neuroimmune communication and epithelial remodeling, positioning it as a potential therapeutic target.
key_finding_ja: IL-25はタフト細胞とILC2の相互作用や神経免疫連関を通じて、腸管寄生虫感染に対する生体防御と組織適応を統合的に制御している。
why_it_matters_ja: IL-25を介した粘膜保護機構の解明は、免疫病理を抑えつつ寄生虫感染症や粘膜疾患を制御する新たな治療標的の同定につながる可能性がある。

title: Citrullination and Deamidation in Type 1 Diabetes: Linking Beta Cell Stress to Neoantigen-Driven Autoimmunity.
abstract: Citrullination and deamidation are post-translational modifications (PTMs) increasingly recognized as important contributors to neoepitope formation in type 1 diabetes (T1D). Under inflammatory and endoplasmic reticulum stress conditions, beta cells activate calcium-dependent peptidylarginine deiminase and transglutaminase enzymes, leading to self-protein modification, altered peptide charge and HLA-binding properties, thereby generating neoepitopes that can be recognized by autoreactive CD4 + and CD8 + T cells. Accumulating evidence from both murine and human studies demonstrates that immune responses against citrullinated and deamidated beta cell proteins are present and increase with disease progression, supporting a role in epitope spreading rather than disease initiation. Although both PTMs are biochemically analogous, their kinetics and regulation are distinct: citrullination appears as an earlier and partly intrinsic response of stressed beta cells, whereas deamidation is more closely associated with sustained inflammation and later disease stages. In parallel, reduced PTM-generating enzyme expression in the thymus may limit central tolerance to modified epitopes, facilitating escape of autoreactive T cells. In this review, we summarize current insights into the biochemical and immunological roles of citrullination and deamidation in T1D, with emphasis on their temporal regulation, contribution to neoepitope formation, and potential as therapeutic targets, highlighting key findings from our own work in the field.
authors: Callebaut A, Bruggeman Y, Mathieu C, James EA, Overbergh L.
screening_reason: The paper focuses directly on protein post-translational modifications (citrullination and deamidation) and their mechanistic role in generating neoepitopes.
summary_ja: 本総説は、1型糖尿病（T1D）におけるタンパク質翻訳後修飾（シトルリン化および脱アミド化）とネオ抗原形成のメカニズムを解説している。炎症や小胞体ストレス下で活性化した酵素により自己タンパク質が修飾され、抗原提示分子への結合性が変化することで自動活性化T細胞が認識するネオエピトープが生じる。シトルリン化はストレスを受けた膵β細胞の初期応答として生じるのに対し、脱アミド化は持続的な炎症や病期の進行とより強く関連している。また、胸腺における修飾酵素の発現低下が中枢性寛容の回避を促進する可能性が指摘されている。
summary_en: This review outlines the roles of post-translational modifications, specifically citrullination and deamidation, in generating neoepitopes during type 1 diabetes progression. Beta cell stress activates modifying enzymes that alter self-proteins, resulting in neoepitopes recognized by autoreactive CD4+ and CD8+ T cells. While citrullination represents an early stress response, deamidation correlates with sustained inflammation in later disease stages.
key_finding_ja: シトルリン化と脱アミド化は異なる時間的制御を受けて膵β細胞のネオ抗原を形成し、1型糖尿病における自己免疫反応の拡大に貢献している。
why_it_matters_ja: 翻訳後修飾に由来するネオ抗原の生成機序を解明することは、1型糖尿病の早期診断マーカーや特異的免疫療法の開発に寄与する可能性がある。

title: β-hydroxybutyrate regulates microglia M1/M2 polarization and phagocytosis through the JAK1/STAT1 pathway to reduce neuroinflammation and exert anti-epileptic effects.
abstract: Neuroinflammation and microglia M1/M2 polarization imbalance are among the core pathological mechanisms of epilepsy (EP), with the JAK1/STAT1 pathway being vital in neuroinflammation. β-hydroxybutyrate (BHB), a ketone body metabolite, has anti-inflammatory and neuroprotective potential, but whether it can ameliorate EP-related neurological damage by modulating this pathway remains unclear. To investigate whether BHB regulates microglia polarization and phagocytosis through the JAK1/STAT1 pathway, attenuates neuroinflammation and neuronal injury, and thus exerts anti-EP effects. A rat primary neuronal EP model and lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced M1-type microglia model were constructed, and microglia polarization, migration, phagocytosis, and neuronal damage were detected by scratch assay, flow cytometry, Hoechst 33,342/PI staining, Cell Counting Kit-8 assay, and ELISA kits. A rat model of Pentetrazol (PTZ)-induced EP was constructed to detect the effects of BHB on the symptoms of EP in rats by behavioral assessment, and to detect brain tissue damage by pathological staining. Western blot was conducted to detect microglia polarization markers, neuronal apoptosis, synapse-related proteins, and JAK1/STAT1 pathway-related proteins expression. Pathway specificity was verified using JAK1 overexpression plasmid (OE-JAK1) and STAT1 inhibitor (Fludarabine). BHB concentration-dependently increased EP neuron viability and suppressed M1 polarization induced by LPS, and promoted M2 polarization. BHB also enhanced the migration and phagocytosis of microglia, and reduced pro-inflammatory factor release, which in turn attenuated their pro-inflammatory damage to neurons and protected synaptic integrity, and this effect was linked to its suppression of JAK1/STAT1 pathway activation. Additionally, BHB extended seizure latency, decreased seizure duration, and reduced seizure severity in EP rats, and effectively attenuated brain histopathological damage and promoted neuronal regeneration and axonal repair. Furthermore, BHB was also effective in promoting microglia M2 polarization and enhancing their phagocytosis in vivo. Overexpression of JAK1 attenuated the neuroprotective effects of BHB, and Fludarabine attenuated the impacts of overexpression of JAK1. By inhibiting the JAK1/STAT1 pathway, BHB promotes microglia M2 polarization and enhances their phagocytosis, attenuates neuroinflammation and neuronal injury, and ultimately exerts anti-EP effects.
authors: Yang H, Wang H.
screening_reason: Demonstrates that beta-hydroxybutyrate regulates microglial polarization and phagocytosis via JAK1/STAT1 signaling to suppress neuroinflammation.
summary_ja: てんかんにおける神経炎症とミクログリアのM1/M2分極異常に対するβ-ヒドロキシ酪酸（BHB）の作用機序をラットモデルおよび細胞モデルで解析した。BHBはJAK1/STAT1経路の活性化を抑制することで、LPS誘発性M1分極を抑え、M2分極と貪食能を促進した。さらに、PTZ誘発てんかんラットにおいてBHBは発作潜時の延長や重症度の低下をもたらし、脳組織損傷を軽減した。JAK1の過剰発現はBHBの保護効果を減弱させ、STAT1阻害剤はこの過剰発現の影響を打ち消した。
summary_en: This study investigated the neuroprotective effects of beta-hydroxybutyrate (BHB) in rat epilepsy models and microglial cell cultures. BHB promoted microglial M2 polarization, enhanced phagocytosis, and suppressed neuroinflammation by inhibiting the JAK1/STAT1 pathway. In vivo, BHB reduced seizure severity and brain histopathological damage, which was attenuated by JAK1 overexpression.
key_finding_ja: β-ヒドロキシ酪酸はJAK1/STAT1経路を抑制することでミクログリアのM2極性化と貪食能を促進し、神経炎症およびてんかん症状を軽減した。
why_it_matters_ja: BHBによるミクログリア極性化の制御機構の解明は、てんかんにおける神経炎症を標的とした新たな治療法の開発につながる可能性がある。

title: The emerging role of endoscopy in neurogastroenterology.
abstract: Purpose of review Purpose of the review is provision of an up-to-date literature review on the growing importance of endoscopy in neurogastroenterology and its limitations. Recent findings Traditionally, the diagnostic role of endoscopy in neurogastroenterology lies in the initial suspicion of motility disorders and exclusion of important differential diagnoses. Endoscopy may serve also as a carrier for positioning examination devices such as the Bravo reflux-capsule to proof gastroesophageal reflux or the endoluminal functional lumen imaging probe (EndoFLIP). New interesting aspects are the resection-based and biopsy-based extraction of tissue for examination of the enteric nervous system by the full thickness resection device (FTRD) to detect structural gastrointestinal neuromuscular lesion and confocal laser endomicroscopy (CLE) to investigate potential correlations for food intolerance. Effectiveness of endoscopic therapy is dependent on whether the measured circumscribed dysfunction correlates with the symptoms and explains them. This is the case in esophageal achalasia and hypercontractile motility disorders. However, in gastropareses, the significance of endoscopic therapy is limited because of its complex pathophysiology. Summary There is an emerging role of endoscopy in neurogastroenetrology. However, effectiveness of endoscopic therapy is dependent on careful patient selection and evidence of a circumscribed dysfunction that correlates with the symptoms and explains them.
authors: Frieling T.
screening_reason: Discusses endoscopic techniques for tissue extraction and examination of the enteric nervous system and GI motility in neurogastroenterology.
summary_ja: 神経消化器病学における内視鏡検査の新たな役割とその限界について文献レビューが行われた。内視鏡はアカラシア等の運動障害の診断補助やBravoカプセル、EndoFLIPなどの検査機器の留置に用いられている。さらに、全層生検による腸管神経系の評価や、共焦点レーザー内視鏡を用いた食物不耐症の検討も進んでいる。内視鏡治療の有効性は、症状に対応する局所的な機能障害の証明と適切な患者選択に依存することが示されている。
summary_en: This review outlines the evolving role and limitations of endoscopy in neurogastroenterology. Endoscopic methods facilitate the placement of diagnostic devices, tissue extraction for enteric nervous system evaluation, and targeted therapeutic interventions. The clinical effectiveness of endoscopic therapy depends heavily on precise patient selection and demonstrated focal dysfunction correlating with symptoms.
key_finding_ja: 内視鏡検査は運動障害の診断機器留置や腸管神経系の組織採取、局所的障害に対する治療において新たな役割を果たしている。
why_it_matters_ja: 内視鏡技術の発展は消化管運動障害の正確な診断や適切な治療対象患者の選別に寄与する可能性が生じている。

title: Multipathway modulation of neuroinflammation and oxidative stress by hesperidin in a rat single prolonged stress model of post-traumatic stress disorder.
abstract: Background Post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) is a complicated neuropsychiatric disorder that is marked by long-term neuroinflammation, oxidative stress, and poor neuroplasticity in stress-sensitive brain areas. Hesperidin is a citrus-derived flavanone glycoside that has been reported to have multitarget neuroprotective effects with antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and neurotrophic regulatory activities. However, its integrated effects across convergent pathological pathways in validated PTSD models remain insufficiently defined. Methods Male Wistar rats were subjected to the single prolonged stress (SPS) paradigm and treated with hesperidin (50, 100, and 200 mg/kg), fluoxetine (20 mg/kg), or vehicle for 14 days. Biochemical assessments (malondialdehyde [MDA], catalase [CAT], superoxide dismutase [SOD]) and immunohistochemical measurements of neuronal and glial integrity (NeuN, glial fibrillary acidic protein [GFAP], brain-derived neurotrophic factor [BDNF]) in the hippocampus, amygdala, and prefrontal cortex were performed. Results SPS exposure induced marked oxidative imbalance, evidenced by increased MDA levels and reduced CAT activity, alongside significant upregulation of tumor necrosis factor α (TNF-α), interleukin 6 (IL-6), and IL-1β, increased astrocytic reactivity (GFAP), and reduced BDNF expression. Hesperidin treatment significantly attenuated lipid peroxidation, partially restored CAT activity, and suppressed pro-inflammatory cytokines, with the most pronounced effect observed for IL-1β. Notably, hesperidin reduced astrocytic activation and preserved neuronal morphology, while enhancing BDNF expression in a dose-dependent manner, with optimal effects at 50-100 mg/kg. Conversely, there was little group variation in the activity of SOD, implying pathway-selective redox regulation. Conclusion Hesperidin has multipathway, coordinated, modulatory effects on oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, glial activation, and neurotrophic signaling in the SPS model of PTSD. These findings support its utility as a mechanistic probe for interrogating convergent stress-related neuropathological pathways.
authors: Anyanwu GE, Akanaku OC, Oviosun A, Ekwueme PE, Odey PA, Okechukwu Ugwu CP, Anyanwu CN.
screening_reason: Studies the attenuation of neuroinflammation, pro-inflammatory cytokines, and glial reactivity by hesperidin in a PTSD model.
summary_ja: PTSDの単一長時間ストレス（SPS）ラットモデルを用い、ヘスペリジンの神経保護効果と多角的な作用機序を検証した。SPS曝露は酸化ストレスの上昇、炎症性サイトカイン（TNF-α、IL-6、IL-1β）の増加、アストロサイト活性化（GFAP増強）、ならびにBDNF発現の低下を引き起こした。ヘスペリジン投与により、脂質過酸化の抑制、炎症性サイトカインの減少、アストロサイトの活性化抑制、BDNF発現の上昇および神経細胞形態の保持が確認された。
summary_en: This study evaluated the effects of hesperidin in a rat single prolonged stress (SPS) model of post-traumatic stress disorder. SPS exposure induced oxidative stress, pro-inflammatory cytokine expression, astrocytic activation, and reduced BDNF levels across stress-sensitive brain regions. Treatment with hesperidin reduced lipid peroxidation, suppressed inflammatory cytokines, attenuated astrocytic reactivity, and restored BDNF expression in a dose-dependent manner.
key_finding_ja: ヘスペリジンはSPS誘導PTSDモデルにおいて、酸化ストレス、神経炎症、アストロサイトの活性化、ならびにBDNF低下を多角的に改善する。
why_it_matters_ja: ストレス関連精神疾患における病理メカニズムの解明や、新規治療法開発のための薬理学的ツールとしてヘスペリジンの有用性が期待される。

title: From dysbiotic gut to malodorous mouth: targeting microbial metabolism for gastrointestinal type halitosis.
abstract: This article reviews the microbiological mechanisms of halitosis, the oral-gut axis, the role of the gut microbiome, related metabolic pathways, and their associations with gastrointestinal diseases, and explores intervention strategies based on microbial regulation. Halitosis is primarily caused by volatile sulfur compounds produced by oral microorganisms, especially gram-negative anaerobic bacteria, and volatile organic compounds in most extraoral etiologies. Studies have found that intestinal microbial dysregulation can affect the composition of oral flora through the oral-gut axis and aggravate bad breath. Gastrointestinal diseases, such as gastroesophageal reflux disease, Helicobacter pylori infection, ulcerative colitis and irritable bowel syndrome can directly or indirectly promote the occurrence of bad breath by changing the intestinal microenvironment and microbial metabolic pathways, such as protein spoilage or short-chain fatty acids imbalance, etc. For microbial interventions, traditional Chinese medicine can not only systemically regulate the oral-gut axis balance, but also effectively alleviate bad breath by targeting sterilization and inhibiting the metabolic activity of pathogenic bacteria. This review focuses on elucidating the complex links between halitosis and the gut microbiome, its metabolic pathways, and gastrointestinal diseases, emphasizing the key role of microbial metabolites in pathological mechanisms. It reveals the importance of the oral-gut axis in systemic health and provides a rationale for developing personalized halitosis management strategies based on microbiome regulation.
authors: Liang X, Deng Y, Zhao L, Zhou X, Li Z, Xiao G, Chen S.
screening_reason: The review focuses on the gut microbiome, microbial metabolism, and the gut-oral axis in gastrointestinal conditions.
summary_ja: 本論文は、口臭（口臭症）と腸内細菌叢、微生物代謝産物、および消化器疾患との関連について論じた総説である。腸内細菌叢の乱れは口腔-腸軸を通じて口腔内菌叢の構成や短鎖脂肪酸等の代謝バランスを変化させ、口臭を増悪させることが知られている。逆流性食道炎やヘリコバクター・ピロリ感染症などの胃腸疾患は、腸内環境を変化させることで口臭発生に寄与する。本総説では微生物代謝の観点から口臭の病態を整理し、漢方薬など微生物調節を標的とした介入の可能性を議論している。
summary_en: This review highlights the interplay between the gut microbiome, microbial metabolic pathways, and halitosis via the oral-gut axis. Dysbiosis and gastrointestinal disorders alter microbial metabolites such as volatile sulfur compounds and short-chain fatty acids, contributing to bad breath. The authors discuss potential microbiome-targeted interventions, including traditional Chinese medicine, for managing gastrointestinal-associated halitosis.
key_finding_ja: 腸内細菌叢の乱れと代謝産物の変動が口腔-腸軸を介して口臭や消化器疾患の病態に関与していることが示された。
why_it_matters_ja: 微生物代謝や口腔-腸軸を標的とした個別化アプローチは、口臭および関連する消化器不調の管理に新たな選択肢をもたらす可能性がある。

title: Exercise-Mediated Modulation of the NLRP3 Inflammasome in Aging and Neurodegenerative Diseases: Mechanisms, Microglial Crosstalk, and Translational Perspectives.
abstract: Regular engagement in physical exercise has been recognized as a formidable non-pharmacological intervention aimed at mitigating age-associated neuroinflammation and neurodegenerative phenomena. A fundamental mechanism that underpins these advantageous effects pertains to the modulation of the NLRP3 inflammasome, which serves as a pivotal regulator of innate immune responses within microglial cells. The aging process is marked by a state of chronic low-grade inflammation, commonly referred to as "inflammaging," which is instigated by mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative stress, and metabolic disturbances; these factors collectively facilitate the activation of NLRP3 and the subsequent secretion of pro-inflammatory cytokines, notably IL-1β. Contemporary research findings suggest that physical exercise diminishes NLRP3 inflammasome activation through various interrelated pathways. These pathways encompass the reduction of reactive oxygen species production, the inhibition of TXNIP-mediated assembly of the inflammasome, and the modulation of metabolites derived from the gut, such as trimethylamine N-oxide. In addition, factors circulating as a result of exercise, which include irisin and meteorin-like protein, play a significant role in promoting systemic and central anti-inflammatory responses, thereby impacting the functional dynamics of microglia. In experimental paradigms investigating the phenomena of aging and neurodegenerative disorders (NDDs), notably Alzheimer's and Parkinson's diseases, physical activity has been shown to diminish amyloid accumulation, tau pathology, and microglial activation, primarily through the attenuation of NLRP3 signaling pathways. Collectively, these observations underscore the role of exercise as a pivotal regulator of neuroimmune equilibrium, thereby providing mechanistic elucidation of its potential therapeutic efficacy in alleviating inflammaging and decelerating the progression of NDDs.
authors: Zhang Y.
screening_reason: The review centers on exercise-induced regulation of the NLRP3 inflammasome, microglial activation, and neuroimmune equilibrium in neurodegenerative diseases.
summary_ja: 本論文は、加齢や神経変性疾患における有酸素運動・身体活動によるNLRP3インフラマソームの調節機構について概説した総説である。加齢に伴う慢性的な微小炎症（インフラメイジング）では、ミクログリアのNLRP3インフラマソームが活性化されプロ炎症性サイトカインが分泌される。運動は活性酸素種の減少や循環因子、腸内細菌由来代謝産物の修飾を介してNLRP3の活性化を抑制し、ミクログリアの活性化を軽減する。実験モデルでは、運動がアミロイド蓄積やタウ病理を抑制し、神経免疫の平衡維持に寄与することが示されている。
summary_en: This review highlights how physical exercise regulates the NLRP3 inflammasome in microglia to suppress age-related neuroinflammation and neurodegenerative pathology. Exercise reduces ROS production, influences circulating factors and gut-derived metabolites, and attenuates amyloid and tau pathology in experimental models. These findings emphasize physical activity as a key non-pharmacological modulator of neuroimmune equilibrium.
key_finding_ja: 運動はNLRP3インフラマソームの活性化を抑制することでミクログリアの炎症応答を減弱させ、神経変性疾患の病理変化を軽減する。
why_it_matters_ja: 運動によるミクログリア活性化抑制の分子メカニズム解明は、加齢性神経変性疾患に対する非薬物療法の理論的基盤を強化する可能性がある。

title: Cross-link Between CircRNAs and Neuroinflammation in Parkinson's Disease.
abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a major neurodegenerative disorder affecting a large number of people worldwide. PD has been characterized by motor abnormalities, as well as non-motor abnormalities that lower patients' quality of life. The pathological features of PD include the substantia nigra's dopaminergic neurons degradation, leading to a progressive clinical course, Lewy bodies and Lewy neurites, which are primarily composed of α-synuclein, and chronic neuroinflammatory changes that contribute to disease progression. Circular RNAs (circRNAs) are a type of circular single-stranded RNAs possessing high stability. Their expression varies depending on tissue type, cell type, and developmental stage, suggesting their roles in regulating biological processes. Recent research has indicated that circRNAs participate in PD pathophysiology by modulating neuroinflammation, immune response, mitochondrial dysfunction, and reactive oxygen species accumulation. Mechanistically, many circRNAs appear to act as molecular sponges for microRNAs, thereby influencing the expression of key genes involved in inflammatory signaling, synaptic regulation, and neuronal survival. This review summarizes the impact of circRNAs on neuroinflammation, astrocyte/microglia dysfunction, mitochondrial damage, and oxidative stress in PD. It also summarizes experimental evidence from cellular and animal models showing that multiple circRNAs can modulate inflammatory pathways in PD and related neurological disorders. However, only a limited number of studies have evaluated circRNAs as biomarkers or therapeutic targets in patient samples, and comprehensive in vivo validation of circRNA-miRNA-target network remains insufficient. A better understanding of these regulatory pathways may help identify clinically relevant biomarkers and support the development of circRNA-based therapeutic strategies for PD.
authors: El-Ashmawy NE, Khedr EG, Darwish RT, Ibrahim AO.
screening_reason: The review focuses on the central role of circRNAs in modulating neuroinflammation and microglial/astrocytic activation in Parkinson's disease.
summary_ja: 本論文は、パーキンソン病（PD）の病態生理における環状RNA（circRNA）と神経炎症の相互作用についてまとめた総説である。circRNAは高安定な環状単一鎖RNAであり、microRNAの分子スポンジとして機能することで炎症シグナル伝達や神経細胞の生存に関わる遺伝子発現を調節する。細胞モデルや動物モデルの研究から、複数のcircRNAがミクログリアやアストロサイトの機能異常、ミトコンドリア障害、酸化ストレスを制御することが示されている。しかし、患者検体におけるバイオマーカーや治療標的としての検証、ならびに生体内での調節ネットワークの網羅的解析はまだ不十分である。
summary_en: This review discusses the role of circular RNAs (circRNAs) in modulating neuroinflammation, immune responses, and cellular stress in Parkinson's disease (PD). CircRNAs function primarily as microRNA sponges, thereby regulating key signaling pathways involved in glial cell dysfunction and neuronal survival. Although functional evidence from cellular and animal models shows circRNAs can attenuate neuroinflammation, further in vivo validation and clinical evaluation in patient samples are needed.
key_finding_ja: circRNAはmicroRNAのスポンジとして機能し、パーキンソン病モデルにおいて神経炎症や神経細胞障害を制御することが明らかとなった。
why_it_matters_ja: circRNAを介した神経炎症の調節機構の解明は、パーキンソン病に対する新たな診断バイオマーカーや治療戦略の開発につながる可能性がある。

title: p-Coumaric Acid Attenuates Lead Acetate-induced Neurotoxicity in Rats by Improving Behavioral Dysfunction and Suppressing Oxidative Stress, Neuroinflammation, Apoptosis, and Plasticity-related Molecular Alterations.
abstract: This study evaluated the neuroprotective effects of p-coumaric acid (p-CA) against lead acetate (PbAc)-induced neurotoxicity in rats by focusing on oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, apoptosis, and neuronal plasticity. 35 male rats were randomly assigned to five groups: Control, p-CA (100 mg/kg), PbAc (30 mg/kg), PbAc + p-CA (50 mg/kg), and PbAc + p-CA (100 mg/kg). Treatments were administered orally for 14 days. Behavioral performance was assessed using the open field test (OFT) and elevated plus maze (EPM). Biochemical analyses of brain tissue included the measurement of MDA, GSH, SOD, CAT, and GPx levels. Western blotting was performed to determine the protein expression levels of inflammatory, glial, and synaptic markers, including NF-κB, IL-1β, IL-6, TNF-α, Iba-1, GFAP, PSD-95, and AChE. Quantitative real-time PCR was used to assess the mRNA expression levels of Bax, Bcl-2, Caspase-3, MAP-2, NeuN, and GAP-43. Histological evaluations included hematoxylin-eosin (H&E) staining for neuronal morphology, immunohistochemistry (IHC) for 8-OHdG, GABA, and GFAP, and immunofluorescence (IF) staining for BDNF expression. PbAc exposure caused marked oxidative damage, neuroinflammatory activation, enhanced apoptotic signaling, and impaired neuronal plasticity, accompanied by reduced antioxidant defenses and altered expression of plasticity-related markers. Co-treatment with p-CA significantly ameliorated these biochemical, molecular, and histopathological alterations in a dose-dependent manner. The 100 mg/kg dose of p-CA showed the strongest neuroprotective effect, restoring many parameters close to control levels. Overall, these findings suggest that p-coumaric acid exerts neuroprotective effects against PbAc-induced brain injury by attenuating oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, and apoptosis while supporting neuronal plasticity. Therefore, p-CA may represent a promising natural compound for further investigation in heavy metal-induced neurotoxicity models. However, further studies are required to clarify the upstream molecular signaling pathways involved and to determine whether these protective effects can be maintained under long-term exposure conditions.
authors: Karaarslan T, Bolat M, Bolat İ, Orhan B, Senocak EA, Tekin S, Lacin BB, Golgeli A, Atasever A.
screening_reason: The study directly investigates the attenuation of lead-induced neuroinflammation and inflammatory protein markers in a rat model.
summary_ja: 酢酸鉛により誘導される神経毒性ラットモデルにおけるp-クマル酸（p-CA）の保護効果を評価した。14日間の経口投与により、鉛暴露に伴う行動障害、酸化ストレス、アポトーシス、および神経炎症マーカーの上昇が用量依存的に抑制された。さらに、シナプス可塑性関連タンパク質や遺伝子の発現低下が改善され、100 mg/kg群で最も高い効果が認められた。
summary_en: This study evaluated the neuroprotective effects of p-coumaric acid (p-CA) against lead acetate-induced neurotoxicity in rats. Oral administration of p-CA for 14 days dose-dependently reduced oxidative stress, apoptosis, and neuroinflammatory markers while improving behavioral deficits and synaptic plasticity parameters. The 100 mg/kg dose demonstrated the strongest protective action, restoring multiple biomarkers close to control levels.
key_finding_ja: p-クマル酸は酸化ストレス、神経炎症、アポトーシスを抑制し、酢酸鉛によるラットの神経毒性を軽減した。
why_it_matters_ja: 重金属中毒による脳障害や神経炎症を軽減するための天然由来化合物としての可能性が示唆される。

title: The role of PANoptosis regulatory networks in acute neurological injury.
abstract: Secondary injury following acute neurological insults-including stroke, spinal cord injury(SCI), traumatic brain injury(TBI), and subarachnoid hemorrhage(SAH)-is a major contributor to neuronal death and neuroinflammation; however, the complex molecular mechanisms driving these pathological processes remain poorly understood. The limited efficacy of traditional apoptosis-targeted therapies highlights the need to investigate alternative regulated cell death pathways governed by diverse and intricate regulatory networks. PANoptosis, an emerging form of inflammatory programmed cell death initially proposed to describe the crosstalk among apoptosis, pyroptosis, and necroptosis, is regulated by dynamic molecular complexes, such as the PANoptosome, which orchestrate multiple cell death-associated pathways and contribute to neuronal loss and the amplification of inflammatory responses. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the molecular mechanisms of PANoptosis and its functional roles in acute neurological injury, with a particular emphasis on its pathological regulatory networks associated with ischemic stroke and spinal cord injury. Furthermore, we highlight emerging therapeutic strategies targeting PANoptosis. Recent evidence has identified key molecular mediators, including Z-DNA-binding Protein 1 (ZBP1), receptor-Interacting Protein Kinase 1 (RIPK1), and TGF-β-Activated Kinase 1 (TAK1), which regulate PANoptosome assembly and downstream effector pathways, highlighting their potential as promising therapeutic targets. Inhibition of PANoptosis has been shown to markedly alleviate blood-brain barrier (BBB) disruption and neurological deficits. Additionally, this review addresses the translational challenges and future research directions in targeting PANoptosis, providing a theoretical basis for the development of multi-targeted neuroprotective strategies. FACTS: PANoptosis integrates pyroptosis, apoptosis, and necroptosis via PANoptosome associated signaling. ZBP1, RIPK1, and TAK1 are key regulators of PANoptosis in acute neurological injury models. Inhibition of PANoptosis attenuates BBB disruption and improves functional recovery. OPEN QUESTIONS: How do PANoptosome subtypes differ among CNS cell types? Can PANoptosis-specific biomarkers be validated for clinical use? What are the optimal multi-target strategies for inhibiting PANoptosis without compromising immunity?
authors: Gao Z, Wang C, Yang W, Deng Z, Cao Y, Wang M, Wu Y, Shi S, Wang L, Kang H.
screening_reason: Reviews PANoptosis regulatory networks driving cell death and neuroinflammation in acute neurological injuries.
summary_ja: 急性神経傷害における制御された細胞死プログラムであるPANoptosisの分子メカニズムと役割に関するレビューである。PANoptosisはアポトーシス、ピロトーシス、ネクロトーシスが相互作用する炎症性細胞死であり、PANoptosomeによって調節される。ZBP1、RIPK1、TAK1などの分子がPANoptosomeの形成や下流シグナルを規制する主要な因子として特定されている。PANoptosisの抑制は血液脳関門の破綻や神経機能障害を軽減することが示されている。
summary_en: This review summarizes the regulatory networks and functional roles of PANoptosis in acute neurological injuries such as ischemic stroke and spinal cord injury. Key molecular mediators, including ZBP1, RIPK1, and TAK1, orchestrate PANoptosome assembly and drive neuroinflammation and neuronal death. Inhibiting PANoptosis has been shown to attenuate blood-brain barrier disruption and improve functional recovery in acute injury models.
key_finding_ja: ZBP1やRIPK1、TAK1によって調節されるPANoptosisの抑制が、急性神経傷害モデルにおいて血液脳関門の保護や機能回復をもたらすことが示された。
why_it_matters_ja: PANoptosisを標的とした治療戦略は、急性神経傷害後の神経炎症や組織損傷を低減させる新たな選択肢となる可能性がある。

title: RanBP2 promotes ferroptosis resistance and compromises therapeutic response by stabilizing SLC7A1 through LRSAM1 SUMOylation and ubiquitination in lung adenocarcinoma.
abstract: SUMOylation is characterized as a ubiquitin-like post-translational modification that exhibits mechanistic similarities with ubiquitination. Importantly, it modulates the ubiquitination levels of some target proteins, thereby influencing protein stability. Dysregulation of this modification pathway plays a pivotal role in the pathogenesis and progression of various tumors. While recent studies have demonstrated that protein SUMOylation regulates tumor progression, the specific function and mechanism of Ran-binding protein 2 (RanBP2), an E3 SUMO ligase, remain to be elucidated in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD). This study demonstrates that RanBP2 exhibits elevated expression in LUAD and correlates with poor prognosis. Functionally, RanBP2 inhibits ferroptosis and enhances the growth of LUAD cells. Mechanistically, RanBP2 augments the SUMOylation of E3 ubiquitin ligase leucine-rich repeat and sterile alpha motif-containing protein 1 (LRSAM1), facilitating its subsequent degradation in the ubiquitin-proteasome pathway, thereby reducing SLC7A11 degradation. The stabilized SLC7A11 protein suppresses ferroptosis and promotes LUAD cell growth. The identified RanBP2 inhibitor, amodiaquine (AQ), in combination with ferroptosis inducer sulfasalazine (SAS), effectively triggered ferroptosis and suppressed LUAD cell growth in vitro and in vivo. This combination enhanced T-cell infiltration and improved anti-PD-1 immunotherapy efficacy. The research identifies a novel RanBP2-LRSAM1-SLC7A11 axis that promotes ferroptosis resistance and LUAD progression. The combination of AQ and SAS represents a promising therapeutic strategy for LUAD.
authors: Guo S, Zeng Y, Zhang Q, Zhao X, Jin H, Li B, Shen M, Yang Q, Yang L.
screening_reason: Provides a mechanistic study of protein post-translational modifications, specifically SUMOylation and ubiquitination governing LRSAM1 and SLC7A11 stability.
summary_ja: 肺腺がん（LUAD）におけるE3 SUMOリガーゼRanBP2の役割および機序を検討した。RanBP2はLUADで過剰発現しており予後不良と相関し、フェロトーシスを抑制してがん細胞の増殖を促進することが示された。分子機序として、RanBP2はE3ユビキチンリガーゼLRSAM1のSUMO化を亢進させて分解を促進し、これによりSLC7A11の分解を免れさせてフェロトーシス抵抗性を誘発する。RanBP2阻害剤とフェロトーシス誘導剤の併用は腫瘍増殖を抑制し免疫療法の効果を向上させた。
summary_en: This study identified the role of the E3 SUMO ligase RanBP2 in driving ferroptosis resistance in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD). RanBP2 enhances the SUMOylation and proteasomal degradation of the E3 ubiquitin ligase LRSAM1, which stabilizes SLC7A11 and inhibits ferroptosis. Pharmacological inhibition of RanBP2 combined with a ferroptosis inducer effectively triggered cell death, inhibited tumor growth, and enhanced anti-PD-1 immunotherapy efficacy in LUAD models.
key_finding_ja: RanBP2はLRSAM1のSUMO化と分解を介してSLC7A11を安定化させ、肺腺がんにおけるフェロトーシス抵抗性と腫瘍伸長を促進する。
why_it_matters_ja: RanBP2を標的とした治療戦略は、フェロトーシス誘導や免疫療法に対する抵抗性を克服する新たな手段となる可能性がある。

title: Mitochondria-enriched BMSC exosomes restore microglia-neuron cross-talk in Parkinson's disease via PINK1/parkin and PI3K/Akt/mTOR pathways.
abstract: Background Mitochondrial dysfunction and neuroinflammation drive dopaminergic neuron loss in Parkinson's disease (PD). While BMSC-derived small extracellular vesicles (BMSC-Exo) are neuroprotective, their ability to repair mitochondrial deficits is limited. We engineered mitochondrial-enriched sEVs (Exo-Mito) to evaluate their effects on microglia-neuron interactions in a PD-relevant model. Methods BMSC-Exo-Mito were characterized via TEM, NTA, and immunoblotting. Their therapeutic efficacy was assessed using an MPP + -induced BV2/SH-SY5Y transwell co-culture model. Assessments included ROS levels, mitochondrial membrane potential, ATP quantification, mitophagy flux, and signaling pathway analysis. Results Exo-Mito significantly restored mitochondrial homeostasis by reducing ROS, preserving membrane potential, and increasing ATP production. Mechanistically, Exo-Mito enhanced PINK1/Parkin-dependent mitophagy and PGC-1alpha/TFAM-mediated biogenesis. In BV2 microglia, Exo-Mito suppressed the NF-kappaB/NLRP3 axis, reduced proinflammatory cytokines, and promoted M2 polarization. In SH-SY5Y cells with dopaminergic phenotype, Exo-Mito was associated with reactivated PI3K/Akt/mTOR signaling, preserved tyrosine hydroxylase expression, and inhibited apoptosis. Functionally, Exo-Mito improved SH-SY5Y cell and restored microglial migratory capacity, showing superior efficacy to unmodified BMSC-Exo. Conclusion Mitochondria-enriched BMSC sEVs protect SH-SY5Y cells by coordinating mitochondrial quality control and modulating neuroinflammation. These findings support Exo-Mito as a promising cell-free therapeutic strategy for Parkinson's disease.
authors: Shi S, Liu R, Liu C, Chen Y, Pan Y, Wang C.
screening_reason: Focuses on restoring microglia-neuron cross-talk and inhibiting neuroinflammation in Parkinson's disease models.
summary_ja: パーキンソン病（PD）モデルにおけるミトコンドリア濃縮骨髄由来幹細胞小細胞外小胞（Exo-Mito）の治療効果をMPP+誘発BV2/SH-SY5Y共培養系で評価した。Exo-MitoはROS減少やATP産生増大を通じてミトコンドリアの恒常性を回復させ、マイトファジーおよびミトコンドリア生合成を促進した。さらに、BV2ミクログリアの抗炎症化を誘導し、SH-SY5Y細胞のPI3K/Akt/mTOR経路を再活性化してアポトーシスを抑制した。
summary_en: Engineered mitochondria-enriched BMSC extracellular vesicles (Exo-Mito) were evaluated in an MPP+-induced BV2/SH-SY5Y co-culture model of Parkinson's disease. Exo-Mito restored mitochondrial homeostasis by reducing ROS and enhancing PINK1/Parkin-mediated mitophagy and mitochondrial biogenesis. In addition, Exo-Mito suppressed microglial inflammatory responses, promoted M2 polarization, and rescued dopaminergic SH-SY5Y cells through reactivation of PI3K/Akt/mTOR signaling.
key_finding_ja: ミトコンドリア濃縮BMSC小外小胞は、ミトコンドリア品質管理の調節と神経炎症の抑制を通じてミクログリアと神経細胞間の相互作用を修復しドパミン作動性細胞を保護する。
why_it_matters_ja: 無細胞治療法としてのExo-Mitoは、ミトコンドリア障害と神経炎症が関与するパーキンソン病の新しい治療アプローチとなる可能性がある。

title: Liquiritigenin attenuates high-salt diet-induced neuroinflammation, mitochondrial dysfunction, and cognitive impairment via NF-κB pathway inhibition.
abstract: Liquiritigenin (LG), a flavonoid compound extracted from licorice, possesses diverse pharmacological activities, including anti-inflammatory and antioxidant effects. A high-salt diet (HSD) is a common dietary risk factor associated not only with hypertension but also with central nervous system injury. However, the underlying mechanisms and potential therapeutic interventions remain insufficiently explored. In this study, we investigated the neuroprotective effects of LG against HSD-induced brain pathology and cognitive impairment in mice. The mechanism of action was further examined using NaCl-treated HT22 cells with LG intervention. By establishing HSD-related mouse and cellular models, administering different doses of LG, and performing neurobehavioral assessments, we evaluated its effects on brain tissue structure, cognitive performance, neuroinflammation, and mitochondrial function. The results demonstrated that in HSD-fed mice, LG attenuated hippocampal neuronal atrophy and death, thereby improving brain tissue morphology. Behavioral testing further revealed that LG enhanced motor performance and exploratory behavior, alleviating cognitive deficits. At the molecular level, LG reduced the expression of pro-inflammatory mediators while upregulating anti-inflammatory cytokines, effectively suppressing neuroinflammation. In addition, LG decreased cytoplasmic expression of mitochondrial DNA-related genes (d-loop, cox1, non-numt), increased ATP production, and improved mitochondrial function. Mechanistic studies further indicated that LG inhibits HSD-induced nuclear factor kappa-B p65 phosphorylation, reducing neuroinflammation and mitochondrial dysfunction, whereas NF-κB p65 overexpression abrogated these protective effects. In summary, LG protects against neuroinflammation and mitochondrial impairment by suppressing NF-κB signaling, thereby mitigating neurological dysfunction. These findings suggest that LG holds promise as a potential therapeutic agent for the prevention and treatment of HSD-related neurological disorders.
authors: Liu Y, Xu D, Shi Y, Li X, Li M, Zhang J, Yu X, Peng W, Chen H, Guan X, Dong J.
screening_reason: Evaluates the mechanisms by which liquiritigenin suppresses high-salt diet-induced neuroinflammation and NF-kappaB signaling.
summary_ja: 高塩分食（HSD）誘発性の脳病変および認知機能障害に対するリコリチゲニン（LG）の保護効果と作用機序をマウスおよびHT22細胞を用いて検討した。LG投与は海馬神経細胞の萎縮および死を抑制し、行動テストにおける認知機能や運動能力の低下を改善した。さらに、プロ炎症性因子の発現を抑え、ミトコンドリア機能を向上させるとともに、NF-κB p65のリン酸化を阻害することを示した。
summary_en: This study evaluated the protective effects of liquiritigenin (LG) in high-salt diet (HSD)-induced mouse and cell models of neurological impairment. LG treatment attenuated hippocampal neuronal damage, improved motor and cognitive behaviors, and reduced neuroinflammation. Furthermore, LG restored mitochondrial function and suppressed the NF-κB p65 pathway, counteracting HSD-induced central nervous system injury.
key_finding_ja: リコリチゲニンはNF-κBシグナル伝達を抑制することにより、高塩分食に起因する神経炎症とミトコンドリア障害を軽減し、認知機能を改善する。
why_it_matters_ja: 高塩分食に伴う脳機能障害の予防や治療において、リコリチゲニンが新たな治療薬候補となる可能性が期待される。

title: Gastrointestinal In Situ Self-Assembled Gastrodia Elata Polysaccharide Hydrogel Enables Parkinson's Disease Therapy via Gut-Brain Axis Modulation.
abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is closely associated with abnormal α-synuclein propagation along the gut-brain axis and progressive dopaminergic neuronal loss. Traditional oral preparations suffer from weak gastrointestinal resistance, rapid degradation and poor gut-brain axis regulation. Here, we constructed a gastrodia elata polysaccharide-functionalized dual-network GEPH hydrogel via thiol-maleimide click crosslinking. GEPH possesses favorable biocompatibility, regular porous microstructure and tailored rheological properties suitable for gastrointestinal delivery, showing outstanding erosion resistance and structural stability in simulated intestinal fluid. It achieves in situ gelation in the gastrointestinal tract and maintains 24 h long-term retention after oral administration. GEPH modulates gut microbiota composition and metabolite profiles, repairs intestinal barrier and neuronal injury in PD mice such as Corynebacterium, CAG_95, and Akkermansia, while regulated metabolite abundance such as 3-methyl-4-cis-hydroxy-2-butenal, Nicotinic acid, Linolenate. By regulating the TLR4/NF-κB pathway and gut-brain axis, it inhibits abnormal aggregation and spread of intestinal and cerebral α-synuclein, alleviates neuroinflammation and neuronal apoptosis, protects dopaminergic neurons and ameliorates motor dysfunction. This study proposes GEPH as a new type of oral functionalized dual-network hydrogel formulation that regulates the gut-brain axis, promoting the clinical application of a new strategy for oral drug administration for gastrointestinal prevention and treatment of PD.
authors: Lei T, Yang X, Fu G, Li G, Wu Y, Xue X, Zhao Y, Zhang S, Li T, Yang H.
screening_reason: Studies oral hydrogel modulation of gut microbiota composition, the gut-brain axis, and neuroinflammation in a Parkinson's disease model.
summary_ja: 本研究では、経口投与後に消化管内で自己組織化する天麻多糖機能化ハイドロゲル（GEPH）を開発し、パーキンソン病に対する治療効果を評価した。GEPHは消化管内で24時間保持され、腸内細菌叢の構成や代謝物プロファイルを調節するとともに腸管バリア機能を修復した。さらに、TLR4/NF-κB経路および腸脳相関の調節を介してαシヌクレインの異常集積や伝播を抑制した。その結果、神経炎症やドパミン作動性神経の脱落が軽減され、運動機能障害が改善した。
summary_en: Researchers developed a Gastrodia elata polysaccharide-functionalized hydrogel (GEPH) that self-assembles in the gastrointestinal tract and is retained for 24 hours after oral administration. In a Parkinson's disease mouse model, GEPH modulated gut microbiota composition and metabolite profiles, repaired the intestinal barrier, and inhibited alpha-synuclein aggregation. Through TLR4/NF-kB and gut-brain axis regulation, GEPH reduced neuroinflammation and attenuated motor dysfunction.
key_finding_ja: 消化管内で自己組織化する天麻多糖ハイドロゲルは、腸内細菌叢および腸脳相関の調節を介してαシヌクレインの蓄積と神経炎症を抑え、パーキンソン病モデルマウスの運動機能を改善した。
why_it_matters_ja: 腸脳相関に着目したハイドロゲル製剤は、パーキンソン病に対する経口ドラッグデリバリーの新たな治療戦略となる可能性がある。

title: Fasudil Attenuates Fluoride-induced Neuronal Synaptic Damage by Inhibiting Microglial Inflammation.
abstract: Exposure to high levels of fluoride in drinking water has been linked to cognitive impairment, but the molecular mechanisms underlying this neurotoxicity are not fully understood. In this study, a subchronic rat model was used to investigate whether fluoride-induced synaptic damage involves RhoA/ROCK pathway-mediated microglial activation and inflammation. The role of fasudil, a specific RhoA/ROCK inhibitor, was also evaluated. The results demonstrated that fluoride activated the RhoA/ROCK cascade, stimulated microglial activation and subsequent release of pro-inflammatory cytokines, and resulted in hippocampal synaptic injury. Conversely, fasudil attenuated these effects by downregulating Iba1, TNF-α, and ROCK2 expression. Taken together, these findings establish that RhoA/ROCK signaling critically mediates fluoride-induced neuroinflammation and synaptic damage, thereby offering a mechanistic basis for assessing the neurotoxic risk of environmental fluoride exposure.
authors: Yang W, Bu K, Ren X, Qin S, Wang S, Chu F, Lu C, Liu Z, Liu J, Zhang Y, Yang X, Gao Y, Sun D, Sun H.
screening_reason: The research directly examines fasudil inhibition of microglial activation and RhoA/ROCK-mediated neuroinflammation in a fluoride toxicity model.
summary_ja: 本研究は、高濃度フッ素曝露による海馬シナプス損傷におけるRhoA/ROCK経路とミクログリア炎症の関与、および阻害剤ファスジルの効果をラットモデルで検証した。フッ素曝露はRhoA/ROCKシグナルを活性化し、ミクログリアの活性化と炎症性サイトカインの放出を引き起こしてシナプス障害を誘導した。一方、選択的RhoA/ROCK阻害剤であるファスジルは、Iba1、TNF-α、ROCK2の発現を低下させることでこれらの有害作用を軽減した。これらの結果は、RhoA/ROCK経路がフッ素誘発性神経炎症とシナプス損傷を制御することを示している。
