summary_en: This study evaluated the effects of fasudil, a RhoA/ROCK inhibitor, on fluoride-induced synaptic damage and microglial inflammation in a subchronic rat model. Fluoride exposure activated the RhoA/ROCK pathway, prompting microglial activation and cytokine release that led to hippocampal synaptic injury. Fasudil administration attenuated these inflammatory and synaptic damages by downregulating Iba1, TNF-alpha, and ROCK2 expression.
key_finding_ja: RhoA/ROCK阻害剤ファスジルは、ミクログリアの活性化と炎症を抑制することでフッ素誘発性の海馬シナプス損傷を軽減した。
why_it_matters_ja: フッ素神経毒性のシグナル伝達機構が明示されたことで、環境化学物質による神経影響の評価や保護戦略の検討に役立つ可能性がある。

title: Extracellular vesicle-mediated immune regulation in central nervous system diseases: Mechanistic insights and exercise interventions.
abstract: Central nervous system (CNS) diseases are major contributors to long-term disability and cognitive impairment, with neuroinflammation and immune dysregulation closely implicated in their pathogenesis. Extracellular vesicles (EVs) are phospholipid bilayer-enclosed membrane vesicles secreted by diverse cell types that mediate communication between the periphery and CNS through the delivery of various bioactive molecules, including proteins, lipids, and non-coding RNA, thereby exerting immunomodulatory functions. Accumulating evidence has demonstrated that EVs contribute to immune regulation during the initiation and progression of CNS diseases by modulating pathological processes, including neuroinflammation, pro-inflammatory polarization of glial cells, NLRP3 inflammasome activation, and pyroptosis. Previous studies have reported that exercise exerts neuroprotective effects in CNS diseases through EVs-mediated immune regulation. This review summarizes and critically evaluates the biological characteristics of EVs, EV-mediated immunoregulatory mechanisms, the roles of EV-mediated immunoregulation in CNS diseases, and exercise interventions, thereby providing theoretical insights into the beneficial effects of exercise on brain health.
authors: Tang S, Lin Q, Tang Y, Geng Y.
screening_reason: The paper focuses directly on extracellular vesicle-mediated immune regulation and neuroinflammation in central nervous system diseases.
summary_ja: 本論文は、中枢神経系（CNS）疾患における細胞外小胞（EV）を介した免疫調節機構と運動介入の役割に関する総説である。EVはタンパク質や非翻訳RNAなどの生体分子を輸送し、神経炎症やグリア細胞のプロ炎症性分化、NLRP3インフラマソーム活性化、ピロトーシスを制御する。さらに、運動がEVの免疫調節作用を通じて神経保護効果を発揮することが実験研究で報告されている。本総説はEVの生物学的特性とCNS疾患での役割を整理し、脳の健康維持に向けた運動介入の論理的根拠を提示している。
summary_en: This review outlines the mechanisms by which extracellular vesicles (EVs) regulate neuroinflammation and immune responses in central nervous system diseases. EVs deliver bioactive molecules that modulate glial polarization, NLRP3 inflammasome activation, and pyroptosis. Additionally, the review summarizes evidence that exercise exerts neuroprotective effects through EV-mediated immunomodulation.
key_finding_ja: 細胞外小胞（EV）は神経炎症やグリア細胞の免疫応答を仲介し、運動介入による神経保護作用の担い手となることが整理された。
why_it_matters_ja: EVを介した神経免疫調節の理解は、CNS疾患における脳保護メカニズムの解明および運動療法の開発に寄与する可能性がある。

title: Esketamine alleviates neuroinflammation and cognitive impairment in male 3xTg-AD mice by regulating the TAOK1/IL-17 axis.
abstract: Beyond its antidepressant effects, esketamine (ESK) has the potential to enhance neuroplasticity, facilitating the reconnection with emotional and cognitive processes, improving social cognition, and promoting resilience. However, not much is known about its role in Alzheimer's disease (AD). This study aims to explore the potential mechanism of ESK in AD treatment. The potential targets of ESK were predicted by bioinformatics analysis, and 3xTg-AD male mice were subjected to adeno-associated virus and ESK treatment. Cognitive ability, neuronal damage, and proinflammatory factors in 3xTg-AD mice were evaluated. An inflammatory model was established by inducing mouse cortical neurons with mouse IL-17A protein. Neuronal viability was assessed after treatment with different concentrations of ESK. TAOK1 knockdown or IL-17RA knockdown was performed on 3xTg-AD mice and neurons. TAOK1 was highly expressed in the cerebral cortex of ESK-treated 3xTg-AD mice. ESK improved IL-17-induced neuronal inflammation and DNA damage in a TAOK1-dependent manner. TAOK1 interacted with IL-17RA. IL-17RA knockdown improved DNA damage and inflammatory responses in cells and alleviated cognitive impairment and neuroinflammation in AD mice. Overall, ESK protects against DNA damage-mediated neuroinflammation by promoting TAOK1 and inhibiting IL-17 signaling, thereby improving cognitive dysfunction in 3xTg-AD mice.
authors: Xu T, Zhang C, Yang Y, Shen Z, Zhong Z.
journal: Canadian journal of physiology and pharmacology
screening_reason: Investigates how esketamine regulates the TAOK1/IL-17 axis to mitigate neuroinflammation and cognitive impairment in an Alzheimer's mouse model.
summary_ja: 本研究は、アルツハイマー病モデルの雄性3xTg-ADマウスを用いて、エスケタミンの神経炎症改善効果およびその作用機序を検証した。エスケタミン投与により大脳皮質でTAOK1の発現が上昇し、TAOK1とIL-17RAの相互作用を介してIL-17誘導性の神経炎症とDNA損傷が抑制された。さらに、IL-17RAのノックダウンはマウスの認知機能障害および神経炎症を軽減した。以上より、エスケタミンはTAOK1の促進とIL-17シグナル阻害を通じて認知機能を改善することが示された。
summary_en: This study investigated the neuroprotective mechanisms of esketamine in a male mouse model of Alzheimer's disease. Esketamine reduced IL-17-induced neuronal inflammation and DNA damage through a mechanism involving high expression of TAOK1 and interaction with IL-17RA. Consequently, esketamine administration or IL-17RA knockdown mitigated cognitive impairment and neuroinflammation in 3xTg-AD mice.
key_finding_ja: エスケタミンはTAOK1の発現促進とIL-17シグナル阻害を介して、アルツハイマー病モデルマウスの神経炎症と認知機能障害を改善した。
why_it_matters_ja: アルツハイマー病に伴う神経炎症を標的とした新たな薬物療法の機序解明に寄与する可能性がある。

title: A Vagal-Renal-Splenic Reflex Suppresses Renal Sympathetic Nerve Activity and Preserves Kidney Function After Ischemic Injury.
abstract: Background Acute kidney injury (AKI) is associated with maladaptive increases in renal sympathetic nerve activity (RSNA) and frequently progresses to chronic kidney disease. Neuromodulatory strategies that suppress sympathetic outflow may provide therapeutic benefit. We tested whether afferent vagus nerve stimulation mitigates ischemic AKI by modulating renal sympathetic nerve activity through central autonomic circuits and splenic neuroimmune signaling. Methods Retrograde transsynaptic pseudorabies virus tracing was used to identify neural pathways linking the kidney to vagal sensory circuits in C57BL/6J mice. RSNA, arterial pressure, and heart rate were recorded during intermittent afferent vagus nerve stimulation. Bilateral renal ischemia-reperfusion injury (IRI) was used to assess therapeutic efficacy. Mechanistic studies included subdiaphragmatic vagotomy, renal denervation controls, splenectomy, ganglionic blockade and c-Fos mapping. Results Pseudorabies virus tracing identified polysynaptic pathways linking the kidney to nodose ganglia, dorsal root ganglia, and central autonomic nuclei, with controls supporting tracer specificity. Afferent vagus nerve stimulation (aVNS) produced frequency-dependent and sustained suppression of RSNA. In IRI, aVNS attenuated RSNA surges, preserved GFR, reduced tubular injury markers including NGAL and KIM-1, and limited fibrosis. Protection was observed with both preconditioning and delayed treatment, including stimulation initiated up to 72 hours after injury. Ganglionic blockade abolished acute aVNS responses. Splenectomy eliminated the full RSNA-lowering and renoprotective effects of aVNS, while aVNS reduced systemic norepinephrine and altered splenic signaling. Conclusions Afferent vagus nerve stimulation engages kidney-associated vagal-autonomic pathways that suppress renal sympathetic nerve activity and require splenic signaling for full renoprotection after ischemic AKI.
authors: Mohammed M, Ekperikpe U, Nair SS, Lazartigues E, Tewari AK, Padanilam BJ.
journal: Journal of the American Society of Nephrology : JASN
screening_reason: Identifies a vagal-autonomic-splenic neuroimmune reflex circuit that modulates sympathetic outflow and tissue injury.
summary_ja: 急性腎障害は腎交感神経活動の過剰な上昇を伴い、慢性腎臓病へと進行しやすいことが知られています。本研究ではマウスモデルを用い、求心性迷走神経刺激が腎交感神経活動および虚血再灌流障害に与える影響を検証しました。その結果、求心性迷走神経刺激は腎交感神経活動を持続的に抑制し、虚血後の腎機能低下や組織の線維化を軽減することが明らかになりました。さらに脾臓摘出によってこの保護効果および神経抑制効果が消失したことから、脾臓を介した神経免疫シグナル伝達の重要性が示されました。
summary_en: This study investigated whether afferent vagus nerve stimulation mitigates ischemic acute kidney injury by modulating renal sympathetic nerve activity through central autonomic circuits. In mice, stimulation suppressed renal sympathetic nerve activity, preserved kidney function, and reduced tubular injury and fibrosis after ischemia-reperfusion. These protective effects required splenic signaling, highlighting a kidney-associated vagal-splenic neuroimmune pathway.
key_finding_ja: 求心性迷走神経刺激は腎交感神経活動を抑制し、脾臓を介した神経免疫経路を通じて虚血性腎障害を軽減する。
why_it_matters_ja: 迷走神経と脾臓を結ぶ自律神経・免疫非侵襲的アプローチの理解は、急性腎障害の進行を防ぐ新たな神経調節療法の開発に貢献する可能性があります。

title: The Dual Roles of Microglia- and Astrocyte-Derived Exosomes in Cerebral Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury: from Intercellular Communication to Therapeutic Prospects.
abstract: Cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI) is a complex pathological process characterized by metabolic dysfunction, oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, and structural and functional alterations of the neurovascular unit (NVU). Across different studies, CIRI has been reported to be associated, to varying degrees, with neuronal injury and neurological dysfunction. Increasing evidence suggests that exosomes (EXOs) derived from glial cells, particularly microglia and astrocytes, play critical roles in mediating intercellular communication and regulating injury progression in CIRI. This review systematically summarizes the context-dependent and heterogeneous functions of glia-derived EXOs in CIRI. Microglia-derived EXOs exhibit diverse and context-dependent functions depending on the activation state of donor cells and the surrounding microenvironmental conditions. Under pro-inflammatory conditions, EXOs released from microglia may exacerbate inflammation by carrying cargo components such as circular RNAs (circRNAs) and pro-inflammatory proteins, whereas EXOs associated with reparative states may support tissue recovery through the delivery of functional non-coding RNAs. These cargo components may participate in pathological regulation through multiple signaling pathways. Among them, the nuclear receptor coactivator 4 (NCOA4) axis is associated with ferroptosis, ubiquitin-specific protease 14 (USP14) with proteostasis/apoptosis, and thioredoxin-interacting protein (TXNIP) with inflammasome activity, all of which have been linked to reduced neuronal injury and functional recovery. In addition, M2-type-derived EXOs may participate in the regulation of synaptic plasticity and axonal regeneration by modulating the plexin A2 (PLXNA2)/RhoA/ROCK2 signaling pathway. Astrocyte-derived EXOs (ATC-EXOs) further contribute to NVU regulation. A2-type-derived EXOs have been reported in multiple experimental models to be associated with reduced NLR family pyrin domain containing 3 (NLRP3) inflammasome activity and alterations in the PI3K/Akt and MAPK signaling pathways, accompanied by attenuated inflammatory responses and improved blood-brain barrier (BBB) integrity in these models. Some studies suggest that these effects may be related to the transition of microglial phenotypes toward reparative states; however, sufficient in vivo mechanistic evidence supporting their direct regulatory effects remains lacking. In contrast, neurotoxic astrocytes (A1)-derived EXOs exhibit limited or context-dependent effects. Importantly, exosome function is highly state-dependent and cannot be fully explained by simplified pro-inflammatory microglia anti-inflammatory microglia (M1/M2) or A1/A2 paradigms. Moreover, extracellular vesicle heterogeneity and methodological limitations remain major challenges. Despite promising therapeutic potential, including the ability to cross the BBB and enable multi-target regulation, significant barriers to clinical translation persist, such as delivery efficiency, biodistribution, and standardization. Overall, glia-derived EXOs represent a dynamic and multi-level regulatory system in CIRI and a promising platform for precision therapeutic strategies.
authors: Yang Z, Chen H, Zhang Z, Wei X, Han W, Peng T, Zhu D, Liu C.
screening_reason: Reviews microglial and astrocytic extracellular vesicles in mediating neuroinflammation and neurovascular unit signaling during cerebral ischemia.
summary_ja: 脳虚血再灌流障害（CIRI）において、ミクログリアやアストロサイトなどのグリア細胞由来エクソソーム（EXO）が細胞間コミュニケーションにおいて二面的な役割を果たすことがレビューされています。炎症状態のミクログリア由来EXOは炎症反応を悪化させる一方、修復状態のEXOやA2型アストロサイト由来EXOは神経保護や血液脳関門の保護に寄与します。また、NCOA4軸やUSP14、TXNIPなどのシグナル系がEXOの内包物によって調節されることが示されています。しかし、実験モデルの不均一性や評価手法の限界から、臨床応用には送達効率や標準化などの課題が存在します。
summary_en: This review summarizes the dual, context-dependent roles of microglia- and astrocyte-derived exosomes in cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury. Pro-inflammatory glial exosomes can exacerbate neuroinflammation, whereas reparative phenotypes release exosomes that attenuate inflammasome activity and preserve blood-brain barrier integrity. Translational challenges such as vesicle heterogeneity, targeting efficiency, and standardization are also critically addressed.
key_finding_ja: グリア細胞由来エクソソームは、ドナー細胞の活性化状態に応じて脳虚血再灌流障害を悪化または改善する二面的な調節機構を持つことが体系化された。
why_it_matters_ja: グリア細胞由来エクソソームの精密な分子機構理解と標準化は、脳卒中に対する精密医療や新規ドラッグデリバリーシステムの開発に寄与する可能性があります。

title: Recent insights in pathogenesis of endometriosis with focus on gut microbiota.
abstract: EMs is a chronic, estrogen-dependent systemic inflammatory disorder defined by the ectopic implantation of endometrial glands and stroma and is frequently associated with dysmenorrhea, chronic pelvic pain, infertility, and substantial impairment in quality of life. Despite its high prevalence and socioeconomic burden, the etiopathogenesis of EMs remains incompletely elucidated and appears to involve intricate interactions among endocrine dysregulation, immune dysfunction, epigenetic reprogramming, ferroptosis, miRNA-mediated gene regulation, environmental exposures, and lifestyle-related factors. Accumulating evidence has increasingly implicated GM dysbiosis in EMs development and progression. Alterations in microbial diversity and composition have been associated with changes in host immune homeostasis, estrogen metabolism, intestinal barrier integrity, inflammatory signaling cascades, microbial-derived metabolites, and gut-brain axis communication, which may foster a pro-inflammatory pelvic microenvironment that in turn may facilitate lesion implantation, angiogenesis, neuroinflammation, and pain sensitization. Elevated lipopolysaccharide levels, reduced short-chain fatty acid production, Th17/Treg imbalance, macrophage polarization, and epigenetic modulation have also been associated with GM perturbations in EMs. This review synthesizes current advances in understanding the multifactorial mechanisms underlying EMs pathogenesis, with a particular emphasis on microbiota-host interactions. We also discuss emerging microbiota-targeted therapeutic strategies, including probiotics, dietary modulation, and fecal microbiota transplantation, highlighting their translational potential as adjunctive approaches for disease management and personalized medicine in EMs.
authors: Kardan R, Hemmati J, Nazari M, Chegini Z, Ansariniya H.
screening_reason: Focuses on the central role of gut microbiota dysbiosis, microbial metabolites, and gut-brain interactions in endometriosis pathogenesis.
summary_ja: 子宮内膜症（EMs）は異物性の内膜組織が増殖する全身性慢性炎症性疾患であり、その病態には多様な因子が関与しています。近年の研究では、腸内細菌叢の多様性や組成の変化（ディスバイオーシス）が子宮内膜症の発症や進展に関連していることが示されています。腸内細菌叢の異常は、エストロゲン代謝や腸管バリア機能、LPS上昇や短鎖脂肪酸減少を介して骨盤内のプロ炎症性環境を維持し、神経炎症や痛みの増幅に寄与すると考えられています。本レビューでは、腸内細菌と宿主の相互作用メカニズムを整理し、プロバイオティクスや食事療法などの細菌叢ターゲット療法の可能性を論じています。
summary_en: This review synthesizes the multifactorial pathogenesis of endometriosis, with a focus on the key roles played by gut microbiota dysbiosis. Alterations in intestinal microbial composition disrupt host immune homeostasis and estrogen metabolism, facilitating a pro-inflammatory pelvic microenvironment, neuroinflammation, and pain sensitization. Emerging microbiota-targeted interventions such as probiotics and dietary modulation are discussed as novel adjunctive strategies.
key_finding_ja: 腸内細菌叢のディスバイオーシスが、エストロゲン代謝や免疫応答の変更を通じて子宮内膜症の病態形成や神経炎症、痛み増幅に関与していることが総括された。
why_it_matters_ja: 腸内細菌叢を標的とした介入は、子宮内膜症に対する補助的治療や個別化医療の確立に貢献する可能性があります。

title: Microglial 5-LOX-activating protein antagonism alleviates leukotriene-driven neuroinflammation.
abstract: In multiple sclerosis (MS), the chronic, unresolved nature of neuroinflammation within the central nervous system (CNS) remains a major obstacle for effective therapeutic intervention. This challenge arises primarily due to an incomplete understanding of the dysregulated inflammatory and pro-resolving pathways underlying MS lesion progression. Bioactive lipid mediators (LMs), biosynthesized through the coordinated actions of specific enzymes like lipoxygenases (LOX) and cyclooxygenases (COX), are key regulators of both the initiation and resolution of an inflammatory response; however, their spatial organization and functional role during MS pathology have not been fully elucidated. Here, by using pneumatically assisted nanospray desorption electrospray ionization (PA nano-DESI) mass spectrometry imaging and immunohistochemistry, we reveal an increase in the LM leukotriene B 4 (LTB 4 ) in human MS white matter compared to controls, with further enrichment in MS lesions relative to perilesional areas, alongside elevated microglial 5-LOX activating protein (FLAP) expression. Pharmacological antagonism of FLAP suppresses LTB 4 biosynthesis in human-induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived microglia with only marginal effects on the microglia transcriptional phenotype as determined by RNA sequencing. Moreover, in vivo FLAP antagonism ameliorates disease severity and spinal cord inflammatory gene expression in the experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (EAE) model, an animal model of MS, in both a prophylactic and therapeutic settings. This coincided with reduced local LTB 4 biosynthesis and reduced levels of inflammatory monocytes within the spinal cord during EAE. Together these findings establish the FLAP/LTB 4 axis as a driver of neuroinflammation and a druggable therapeutic target for chronic inflammatory CNS disorders like MS.
authors: Konings J, Mingneau F, Chornyi S, Hansen CE, van der Brugt RTM, van Elk TG, Bolkaerts L, Batens B, Tóth G, Lanekoff I, Vaz FM, Cardilli A, Sels M, van der Pol SMA, de Vries HE, Giera M, Werz O, Kessels S, Verberk SGS, Bogie JFJ, Rijnsburger M, Hendriks JJA, Kooij G.
screening_reason: Focuses on microglial FLAP-driven leukotriene biosynthesis as a key neuroinflammatory pathway in multiple sclerosis models.
summary_ja: 多発性硬化症（MS）における持続的な神経炎症の制御には、脂質メディエーターの動態やその合成経路の解明が重要である。本研究は、ヒトMS患者の白質病変部およびヒトiPSC由来ミクログリアを用いて、5-リポキシゲナーゼ活性化タンパク質（FLAP）とロイコトリエンB4（LTB4）の役割を解析した。その結果、MS病変部ではFLAPの発現とLTB4レベルが亢進しており、FLAP拮抗薬の投与によりLTB4生合成が抑制された。さらに、EAEマウスモデルにおいてFLAP拮抗は脊髄における炎症性遺伝子発現や炎症性単球の浸潤を抑え、病勢を改善した。
summary_en: The study evaluated the role of the FLAP/LTB4 axis in neuroinflammation associated with multiple sclerosis using human brain tissue, iPSC-derived microglia, and an EAE mouse model. The authors observed elevated LTB4 levels and microglial FLAP expression in human MS lesions compared to non-disease controls. Pharmacological antagonism of FLAP effectively suppressed LTB4 biosynthesis and reduced clinical severity and spinal cord inflammation in EAE mice.
key_finding_ja: FLAP/LTB4軸の阻害は、ヒトiPSC由来ミクログリアおよびEAEモデルにおいてロイコトリエン生合成と神経炎症を抑制する。
why_it_matters_ja: ロイコトリエン経路を標的としたFLAP拮抗薬が、多発性硬化症などの慢性神経炎症性疾患に対する標的治療につながる可能性を示している。

title: Impact of modified WuMei decoction combined with Bifidobacterium triple viable enteric-coated capsules on clinical efficacy and intestinal microbiota in patients after endoscopic resection of colonic polyps.
abstract: This work was designed to assess the impact of modified WuMei decoction (MWMD) combined with Bifidobacterium triple viable (BTV) enteric-coated capsules on patients following endoscopic resection of colonic polyps. This study enrolled 80 patients with colonic polyps and divided them into a control group and an observation group. Both groups underwent endoscopic polypectomy. The control group received BTV enteric-coated capsules, while the observation group received both BTV enteric-coated capsules and MWMD. Baseline characteristics, postoperative recurrence rates, clinical efficacy, traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) syndrome scores, intestinal microbiota, serum inflammatory cytokines, gastrointestinal quality of life index (GLQI), intestinal mucosa repair, and postoperative complications were compared. Baseline characteristics were similar between the two groups (P > 0.05). At 12 months postoperatively, the observation group demonstrated a lower recurrence rate (P < 0.01) and superior clinical outcomes (P < 0.01). After treatment, TCM symptom scores in this group showed significant improvement (P < 0.05), with a notable reduction in Escherichia coli levels (P < 0.01) and a substantial increase in Bifidobacterium and Lactobacillus counts (P < 0.01). The observation group also exhibited higher GLQI scores (P < 0.01), substantially reduced serum inflammatory markers (P < 0.05, P < 0.01), better intestinal mucosal healing (P < 0.01), and a lower incidence of postoperative complications (P < 0.05). The combination of MWMD and BTV demonstrated good clinical efficacy in patients undergoing endoscopic resection of colonic polyps, promoting intestinal mucosal repair and reducing postoperative complications.
authors: Ye B, Ye W.
journal: Arab journal of gastroenterology : the official publication of the Pan-Arab Association of Gastroenterology
screening_reason: Evaluates the impact of herbal treatment and probiotics on colonic mucosa repair and gut microbiome composition.
summary_ja: 大腸ポリープの内視鏡的切除術を受けた患者80名を対象に、加味烏梅湯（MWMD）とビフィズス菌三種生菌腸溶カプセル（BTV）の併用効果を評価した。併用群では12か月時点のポリープ再発率が有意に低下し、症候スコアおよび臨床成績の改善が見られた。また、ビフィズス菌や乳酸菌の増加と大腸菌の減少が確認され、血清炎症性サイトカインの低下や粘膜修復の促進が観察された。
summary_en: A clinical trial involving 80 patients evaluated the effects of combining modified WuMei decoction (MWMD) with Bifidobacterium triple viable capsules following endoscopic resection of colonic polyps. Combination therapy significantly reduced the 12-month recurrence rate and improved clinical outcome and symptom scores compared to capsules alone. Additionally, the combination promoted intestinal mucosal repair, increased beneficial gut microbiota, reduced Escherichia coli levels, and lowered serum inflammatory cytokines.
key_finding_ja: 大腸ポリープ切除後の患者において、加味烏梅湯とビフィズス菌製剤の併用は再発率を低下させ、腸内細菌叢のバランス改善と粘膜修復を促進した。
why_it_matters_ja: ポリープ切除後の再発予防や腸粘膜保護に対する統合医療的治療法の臨床的有用性を示唆している。

title: Gut microbiome and avascular necrosis: A scoping review of current evidence and knowledge gaps.
abstract: Avascular necrosis (AVN) is a progressive bone disorder characterized by impaired blood supply, osteocyte death, and structural collapse, most commonly affecting the femoral head. In recent years, growing evidence has suggested that gut microbiota may influence skeletal health through immune, metabolic, and vascular pathways. This scoping review aimed to systematically map current evidence on the relationship between gut microbiota and AVN and to identify key knowledge gaps. Following Joanna Briggs Institute methodology and PRISMA-ScR guidelines, a comprehensive search of PubMed, EMBASE, ScienceDirect, Web of Science Core Collection, ClinicalTrials.gov, and Cochrane CENTRAL was conducted. Thirteen eligible studies, including experimental, clinical, multi-omics, and Mendelian randomization analyses, were included. The available evidence indicates that AVN, particularly glucocorticoid- and alcohol-associated forms, is consistently associated with intestinal dysbiosis, reduced production of short-chain fatty acids, immune activation, vascular impairment, and altered bone remodeling. Animal and translational studies demonstrate partial reversal of pathological changes through microbiota-targeted interventions, while human studies reveal etiology-specific microbiota-metabolome signatures. Genetic analyses further support a potential causal contribution of selected microbial taxa and pathways. Overall, current data support the existence of a multidimensional gut-bone axis in AVN. However, most evidence remains indirect - derived from animal models, cross-sectional human studies, and genetic inference rather than from direct interventional testing in patients. Well-designed longitudinal and interventional investigations are needed to clarify causality and therapeutic potential.
authors: Poboży T, Poboży K, Domańska-Poboża J, Kotela A, Konarski W.
screening_reason: Scoping review focusing directly on the relationship between gut microbiome dysbiosis, microbial short-chain fatty acids, and avascular necrosis.
summary_ja: 本スコーピングレビューは、特発性大腿骨頭壊死症などの骨頭壊死（AVN）と腸内細菌叢との関連に関する13件の研究を統合・分析した。AVNは腸内細菌のディスバイオーシス、短鎖脂肪酸の減少、免疫活性化、血管障害などと一貫して関連していることが確認された。動物モデルや遺伝学的解析からは腸内細菌を標的とした介入の有効性が示唆されているが、ヒト患者における直接的な介入検証データは限られている。著者らは、因果関係と治療効果を明らかにするための縦断的・介入的研究の必要性を強調している。
summary_en: This scoping review analyzed 13 studies to map current evidence on the relationship between the gut microbiota and avascular necrosis (AVN). The findings indicate that AVN is consistently associated with intestinal dysbiosis, reduced short-chain fatty acids, immune activation, and vascular impairment. While translational and genetic studies support a gut-bone axis in AVN, direct clinical interventional evidence in human patients remains limited.
key_finding_ja: 骨頭壊死と腸内細菌叢の異常および短鎖脂肪酸の減少との間に関連性が認められたが、ヒトでの直接的な介入研究は不足している。
why_it_matters_ja: 腸-骨軸の解明が進めば、骨頭壊死に対する腸内細菌叢を標的とした新たな予防法や治療法の開発につながる可能性がある。

title: Cytokine-mediated immune-to-brain signaling in neural circuit disorders.
abstract: Neuroinflammation has emerged as a fundamental driver of neural circuit dysfunctions across a spectrum of neurodevelopmental and psychiatric disorders. Beyond classical neuroimmune pathologies, accumulating evidence indicates that systemic inflammatory states - including those elicited by infection, metabolic dysfunction, stress, or peripheral immune activation - induce profound and long-lasting alterations in brain development and function. Cytokines act as critical molecular mediators of this peripheral-to-central immune communication, precisely orchestrating microglial activation in a spatiotemporally restricted manner. Inflammasome-dependent signaling, particularly NLRP3 activation and subsequent cytokine release, has a central role in shaping microglial states during neuroinflammation. Here, we integrate current evidence linking systemic inflammation to microglial cytokine signaling programs and discuss how these cascades shape synaptic development, refinement, and circuit function. Although synapse pruning and cytokine-mediated microglial signaling jointly contribute to circuit remodeling, we highlight cytokine-driven microglial state amplification as a central mechanism linking systemic inflammation to neural circuit instability. We also highlight that specific cytokines can exert direct effects on neuronal populations - independent of microglial intermediates - to context-dependently modulate synaptic efficacy and circuit excitability. Finally, we evaluate the mechanisms linking systemic inflammation to brain dysfunction and highlight emerging translational opportunities, including the therapeutic repurposing of cytokine-targeting and immunomodulatory agents for neuropsychiatric interventions.
authors: Lee Y, Ko J, Um JW.
screening_reason: Focuses directly on cytokine-mediated neuroimmune signaling, microglial activation, and neuroinflammation in neural circuit function.
summary_ja: 本レビューは、全身性炎症やサイトカインを介した免疫-脳シグナル伝達が神経回路障害に与える影響について整理している。サイトカインはミクログリアの状態を空間的・時間的に制御するだけでなく、ニューロンに直接作用してシナプス効力や回路の興奮性を変化させる。炎症性シグナルカスケードとシナプス再編が回路の不安定化につながるメカニズムを概説している。サイトカイン標的治療など、神経精神疾患に対する免疫調節薬の臨床応用の可能性を評価している。
summary_en: This review summarizes how systemic inflammation and cytokine-mediated signaling disrupt neural circuit function in neurodevelopmental and psychiatric disorders. Cytokines orchestrate microglial states and can also act directly on neuronal populations to modulate synaptic efficacy and circuit excitability. The authors evaluate prospective translational opportunities, including immunomodulatory and cytokine-targeting agents for neuropsychiatric conditions.
key_finding_ja: 全身性炎症はサイトカインを介してミクログリアの活性化や神経細胞への直接作用を引き起こし、神経回路の不安定化をもたらす。
why_it_matters_ja: 免疫系と脳神経回路の相互作用の解明は、神経精神疾患に対するサイトカイン標的療法の開発につながる可能性がある。

title: A reproducible three-dimensional model of human brain tissue to investigate physiological and disease-associated microglia phenotypes.
abstract: Stem-cell-based in vitro models offer promising potential to elucidate human brain cell functions and interactions, but limitations in reproducibility, maturation and cell-type diversity persist. Especially, prolonged incorporation of mature microglia and studies of neuroinflammation have proven challenging. Here, we developed a human induced pluripotent stem cell-based three-dimensional cortical brain tissue model (3BTM) containing neurons, astrocytes and microglia with high reproducibility, maturity and viability. 3BTMs show morphological, functional and proteomic maturation of all cell types, leading to high similarity to their in vivo counterparts. Incorporated microglia survive for over 6 months and display mature morphology, functions and gene expression. Importantly, when engineered to model Alzheimer's disease pathology, 3BTMs recapitulate key disease hallmarks, including amyloid deposition, increased phospho-tau levels and neuroinflammation, with microglia shifting their transcriptional landscape to disease-relevant signatures. Treatment of Alzheimer's disease 3BTMs with anti-Aβ immunotherapy cleared deposits and largely reversed disease signatures in glia. Together, our microglia-containing model provides a platform for studying physiological and pathological states of human brain tissue.

screening_reason: Develops a 3D human brain tissue model to study microglial physiological and pathological phenotypes in neuroinflammation.
summary_ja: ヒトiPS細胞から誘導した神経細胞、アストロサイト、ミクログリアを含む再現性の高い3次元皮質脳組織モデルが開発されました。組み込まれたミクログリアは6ヶ月以上生存し、成熟した形態、機能、遺伝子発現パターンを維持しました。アルツハイマー病モデルではアミロイド沈着やリン酸化タウの増加とともに神経炎症が再現され、抗体療法により病理学的変化とグリアの異常な遺伝子変動が改善しました。このモデルはヒト脳の生理的機能や疾患における神経免疫応答を調べるプラットフォームとなります。
summary_en: Researchers developed a reproducible human iPSC-derived 3D cortical brain tissue model containing neurons, astrocytes, and functional microglia that survive for over six months. When engineered to model Alzheimer's disease pathology, the platform recapitulated amyloid deposition, phospho-tau elevation, and neuroinflammation. Furthermore, anti-amyloid immunotherapy cleared deposits and reversed disease-associated glial transcriptional signatures in this system.
key_finding_ja: 長期生存するミクログリアを含むヒト3次元脳組織モデルを確立し、アルツハイマー病様の神経炎症病態および薬物応答の再現に成功した。
why_it_matters_ja: ヒト特異的な神経免疫相互作用の解析や神経変性疾患の病態解明、創薬スクリーニングの精度向上に役立つことが期待されます。

title: New insights on microglial lysosomal acidification: A therapeutic target of neurodegenerative diseases.
abstract: Background Microglia, the resident immune cells of the central nervous system (CNS), maintain brain homeostasis and respond to pathological insults. Microglial dysfunction has been implicated in the pathogenesis of several neurodegenerative diseases, including Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, and multiple sclerosis. Impaired lysosomal function, particularly defective lysosomal acidification, leads to the accumulation of undegraded material, thereby promoting neuroinflammation and neuronal damage. Purpose This review examines the mechanisms governing lysosomal acidification in microglia and evaluates its potential as both a therapeutic target and a prognostic biomarker in neurodegenerative diseases. Methods The literature on microglial lysosomal acidification, lysosomal pH regulation, autophagy, and neurodegeneration was searched in PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science. Relevant mechanistic, preclinical, and translational studies were critically appraised and synthesized. Results Lysosomal acidification is increasingly recognized as a key regulator of microglial function and homeostasis. Defective acidification, driven by dysregulation of the vacuolar H+-ATPase (V-ATPase) proton pump, TFEB/TFE3 signaling pathways, and lysosomal ion channels such as TRPML1 and TMEM175, impairs autophagic flux and substrate degradation, facilitating the accumulation of neurotoxic aggregates including amyloid-β and α-synuclein. Emerging evidence suggests that the degree of microglial lysosomal acidification may serve as a prognostic biomarker for disease progression and therapeutic response. Restoration or enhancement of lysosomal acidification through pharmacological modulation of lysosomal pH, activation of autophagy, or targeting of key regulatory pathways has been shown to re-establish microglial homeostasis, attenuate neuroinflammation, and confer neuroprotection in preclinical models. Conclusion Restoration of microglial lysosomal acidification represents a promising therapeutic strategy for neurodegenerative diseases. A deeper understanding of the molecular mechanisms regulating lysosomal acidification in microglia may facilitate the identification of novel biomarkers and therapeutic targets, ultimately contributing to the development of innovative interventions for neurodegenerative disorders.
authors: Jaganathan R, Vijayakumar S, Chen Y, Ye J, Bakthavatchalam P, Wankar D, Yang C, Iyaswamy A, Li M.
screening_reason: Examines microglial lysosomal function and its direct role in regulating neuroinflammation in neurodegenerative diseases.
summary_ja: ミクログリアのライソゾーム酸化機能は、中枢神経系の恒常性維持や神経変性疾患の病態に重要な役割を果たしています。V-ATPaseやTFEB/TFE3、TRPML1などの調節障害による酸化異常は、オートファジーを低下させ、アミロイドβやαシヌクレインなどの有害タンパク質凝集体の蓄積を促進します。本レビューでは、ミクログリアのライソゾームpH調節機構と、その異常が神経炎症や神経細胞障害へ及ぼす影響を整理しています。さらに、ライソゾーム酸化の回復を狙った薬物投与やオートファジー活性化が、前臨床モデルにおいて神経保護効果を示したことを報告しています。
summary_en: This review examines the molecular mechanisms governing microglial lysosomal acidification and its dysregulation in neurodegenerative diseases. Defective acidification driven by impaired V-ATPase and ion channel signaling leads to autophagic dysfunction and the accumulation of neurotoxic protein aggregates. Pharmacological restoration of microglial lysosomal pH attenuates neuroinflammation and confers neuroprotection in preclinical models.
key_finding_ja: ミクログリアのライソゾーム酸化障害は有害タンパク質凝集体の蓄積と神経炎症を促進し、その酸化機能の回復が前臨床モデルで神経保護効果を示すことが示された。
why_it_matters_ja: ミクログリアのライソゾームpH調節機構の解明は、神経変性疾患に対する新たなバイオマーカーや治療ターゲットの開発につながる可能性があります。

title: Neuron-specific suppression of aberrantly active Toll-NFκB signalling mitigates pathogenic tau hyperphosphorylation via Gsk-3β in Drosophila.
abstract: Chronic brain ailments like Alzheimer's disease and Frontotemporal dementia, together referred to as tauopathies, are strongly influenced by neuroinflammation, an age-associated functional anomaly. Neuroinflammation arising from a dysfunctional innate immune response, such as Toll-NFκB signalling, is implicated in modulating tau pathophysiology, with limited understanding of the molecular mechanisms. Pathogenic hyperphosphorylation of tau and its aggregation into neurotoxic species is considered as a central trigger of tau pathology; however, the mechanistic association between these pathogenic events and the Toll signalling remains largely unexplored. We examined the status of the Toll signalling in Drosophila tauopathy models and evaluated whether its modulation modifies disease severity. We present compelling evidence that neuronal expression of pathogenic human tau causes aberrant activation of the Toll signalling. In line, its additional upregulation further aggravates disease severity, while genetic downregulation of Toll components remarkably alleviates both structural and functional deficits. We subsequently noted that knockdown of the Toll pathway attenuates pathogenic tau hyperphosphorylation in a site-specific manner, largely coinciding with restoration of physiological activity of Gsk-3β/Akt/PP2Ac signalling, a relatively less explored molecular axis in neurons. Our study posits a potential contribution of neuron-intrinsic altered Toll signalling cascade in tau pathogenesis, warranting further exploration of this evolutionarily conserved pathway as a therapeutic target.
authors: Aggarwal P, Sarkar S.
journal: Biochimica et biophysica acta. Molecular basis of disease
screening_reason: Investigates neuronal Toll-NFκB neuroinflammatory signaling and its role in modulating tau hyperphosphorylation.
summary_ja: 本研究は、ショウジョウバエのタウオパチーモデルを用いて、神経細胞におけるToll-NFκBシグナル伝達と病理的タウ過リン酸化の関連を調査した。病理学的人体タウの神経発現によりTollシグナルが異常活性化され、このシグナルをノックダウンすることで構造的・機能的欠損が軽減された。さらに、Toll経路の抑制はGsk-3β/Akt/PP2Acシグナル系の正常な活性を回復させ、特定部位におけるタウの過リン酸化を著しく抑制した。以上の結果は、神経細胞自律的な自然免疫シグナルの異常がタウ病態に関与していることを示している。
summary_en: This study examined the role of Toll-NFκB innate immune signaling in Drosophila models of tauopathy. Neuronal expression of pathogenic human tau induced aberrant Toll activation, whereas genetically suppressing Toll components rescued structural and functional deficits. Knockdown of this pathway attenuated site-specific tau hyperphosphorylation by restoring Gsk-3β/Akt/PP2Ac signaling balance.
key_finding_ja: ショウジョウバエモデルにおいて、神経細胞のToll-NFκBシグナル抑制がGsk-3β活性を介してタウの過リン酸化と病理的障害を軽減した。
why_it_matters_ja: 神経細胞内の固有な免疫シグナル経路とタウ病態のメカニズム解明は、アルツハイマー病などのタウオパチーに対する新たな分子標的治療薬の開発に繋がる可能性がある。

title: Lycium barbarum glycopeptide attenuates ischaemic stroke by inhibiting inflammation via SIRT3-mediated NLRP3 deacetylation.
abstract: Background Inflammatory processes play a critical role in ischaemic stroke. Acetylation of NLRP3 is a key step in amplifying neuroinflammation.(LbGP), a bioactive glycoprotein derived from Lycium barbarum, has anti-inflammatory potential, but its mechanisms in post-stroke neuroinflammation remain unclear. Aim This study aimed to investigate the efficacy and molecular mechanisms of LbGP in alleviating neuroinflammation following ischaemic stroke. Methods A mouse model of middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO)/reperfusion was used to induce focal cerebral ischaemia/reperfusion (I/R) injury. Microglial cells were subjected to oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation. Neurological recovery was assessed by Y-maze and open-field tests. Molecular mechanisms were explored using Western blotting, ELISA, co-immunoprecipitation and immunofluorescence. Results LbGP significantly reduced cerebral infarct volume, attenuated neuroinflammation and improved functional recovery in I/R mice. Mechanistically, LbGP suppressed NLRP3 inflammasome activation through Sirtuin 3-mediated inhibition of NLRP3 acetylation, a finding further validated by exacerbated neuroinflammation in Sirt3-knockout mice. Conclusion This study demonstrates for the first time that LbGP alleviates post-stroke neuroinflammation via Sirt3-mediated deacetylation of NLRP3, thereby disrupting inflammasome activation, and identifies LbGP as a promising therapeutic candidate for ischaemic stroke.
authors: Han B, Ma C, Zhang L, Meng S, Bai M, Yu Z, Duan M, Liu J, Guo J, Shi C, He M, Liu Y.
screening_reason: Examines post-stroke neuroinflammation and the mechanistic regulation of NLRP3 post-translational deacetylation by SIRT3.
summary_ja: クコ多糖糖ペプチド（LbGP）は虚血性脳卒中における抗炎症作用を有することが示唆されているが、その詳細な分子機構は不明であった。本研究では、脳虚血再灌流障害マウスモデルおよび酸素糖剥奪/再酸素化微小膠細胞を用いて、LbGPの治療効果と機序を検証した。実験の結果、LbGPの投与は脳梗塞領域を減少させ、神経炎症の抑制および行動機能の回復を促進した。メカニズムとして、LbGPはSIRT3を介したNLRP3の脱アセチル化を誘導し、NLRP3インフラマソームの活性化を抑制することが明らかになった。
summary_en: This study investigated the therapeutic potential and molecular mechanisms of Lycium barbarum glycopeptide (LbGP) in ischemic stroke using mouse and cell models. The authors demonstrated that LbGP treatment significantly reduced cerebral infarction volume, attenuated neuroinflammation, and improved functional recovery following ischemia/reperfusion injury. Mechanistically, LbGP inhibited NLRP3 inflammasome activation by promoting SIRT3-mediated deacetylation of NLRP3.
key_finding_ja: LbGPはSIRT3を介したNLRP3の脱アセチル化を促進することで、インフラマソーム活性化および虚血後の神経炎症を抑制する。
why_it_matters_ja: タンパク質のアセチル化修飾の調節を介した神経炎症抑制アプローチが、虚血性脳卒中に対する新たな治療選択肢となる可能性が期待される。

title: Citrullination in proteins of the polycomb repressor complex 1.
abstract: The Polycomb repressive complexes can be considered a paradigm of chromatin-based gene regulation in animals. Two of the proteins involved in such complexes are the Ring finger protein 1 (RING1) and the intrinsically disordered protein RING1A and YY1 binding protein (RYBP), which binds to RING1 in some of the Polycomb complexes. Peptidyl arginine iminohydrolases (PADIs) are enzymes involved in the post-translational modification of arginine to citrulline. PADI4, one of the five isoforms of PADI in humans, citrullinates RING1B and RYBP at specific arginines at their C-terminal (Arg231) and N-terminal (Arg53) regions, respectively. In this work, we studied in vitro and in silico whether isolated peptides from each protein, encompassing those wild-type arginines and their citrulline-modified counterparts, were capable of binding to PADI4. The isolated peptides, either in wild-type or modified form, were monomeric and disordered as indicated by far-UV CD and NMR. The affinity constants of peptides for PADI4, as measured by fluorescence, biolayer interferometry (BLI) and isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC), were in the low micromolar range (dissociation constants around 10-20 μM), and the affinities were smaller for the citrullinated variants. Molecular docking simulations showed that the isolated peptides from each protein, either in wild-type form or modified variants, targeted the active site of PADI4, corresponding to the catalytic residue Cys645. These findings suggest that the isolated peptides were capable of binding to the enzyme with affinities similar to those of intact RING1B or RYBP, and that citrullination of the arginines diminished the affinity for the enzyme.
authors: Álvarez-Rodríguez MG, Capone E, Vega S, Rejas V, Rizzuti B, Velazquez-Campoy A, Neira JL.
screening_reason: Focuses on mechanistic biochemical characterization of peptidyl arginine deimination (citrullination), a post-translational protein modification.
summary_ja: 本研究は、Polycomb抑制複合体1（PRC1）の構成タンパク質であるRING1BおよびRYBPに対するPADI4によるシトルリン化修飾とその相互作用を解析した。野生型およびシトルリン化修飾を受けたペプチドを用いたインビトロおよびインシリコ解析により、両ペプチドがPADI4の活性部位にマイクロモルレベルの親和性で結合することが示された。シトルリン化修飾によりPADI4に対する結合親和性は低下することが各種分光学的および熱力学解析から明らかになった。これらの結果は、ペプチド単体でもPRC1構成成分とPADI4との相互作用特性を反映していることを示している。
summary_en: This study evaluated the in vitro and in silico binding of wild-type and citrullinated peptides from RING1B and RYBP to the peptidyl arginine deiminase enzyme PADI4. Both forms of isolated peptides bound to the active site of PADI4 with low micromolar affinity, with citrullination resulting in reduced binding affinity. These findings demonstrate that isolated peptide fragments preserve binding characteristics similar to intact proteins while undergoing citrullination-induced affinity changes.
key_finding_ja: PADI4によるRING1BおよびRYBPのシトルリン化修飾は、酵素に対する基質ペプチドの結合親和性を低下させることがインビトロおよびインシリコ解析で示された。
why_it_matters_ja: クロマチン調節複合体タンパク質の翻訳後修飾メカニズムの解明は、エピジェネティックな遺伝子発現制御の理解を深めるのに役立つ可能性がある。

title: The impact of climatic extreme temperatures on gut microbiome-mediated cardio-metabolic health.
abstract: Climate change increases extreme temperature events, like heat and cold waves. Temperature stress can cause gut dysbiosis, potentially affecting cardiometabolic health. In temperature stress conditions, beneficial microbes like Lactobacillus and Bifidobacterium, and favourable metabolites like short-chain fatty acids are observed to be downregulated, while features like Proteobacteria and Prevotella were found to be upregulated. These alterations may lead to upregulation of lipopolysaccharides, trimethylamine N-oxide, and dysregulation in bile acid metabolism, highlighting this as a potential biomarker for disease risk. Furthermore, we discussed mechanistic pathways potentially impacted, including endothelial dysfunction, gut barrier integrity, and energy homeostasis, that link microbial perturbations to metabolic dysfunction and increased risk of cardiometabolic diseases. Moreover, this review proposes potential therapeutic strategies like faecal microbiota transplantation, probiotic supplementation, nanomedicine, and dietary modulation that target the gut microbiome to alleviate the cardiometabolic risks exacerbated by temperature stress. This is the first review to comprehensively synthesize recent scientific findings on the impact of temperature stress on the gut microbiome across multiple animal models and its potential implications on cardiometabolic health.
authors: Shukla A, Rughwani D, Aditya AK, Ray AK.
screening_reason: The review focuses directly on how temperature stress impacts the gut microbiome, microbial metabolites, and subsequent host cardiometabolic health.
summary_ja: 気候変動に伴う極端な温度変化（寒波や熱波）は、腸内細菌叢の乱れ（ディスバイオシス）を引き起こし、心血管代謝の健康に悪影響を及ぼす可能性があります。温度ストレス下では、乳酸菌やビフィズス菌などの有益な細菌や短鎖脂肪酸が減少する一方、プロテオバクテリアやプレボテラが増加することが報告されています。これにより、リポ多糖やTMAOの上昇、胆汁酸代謝の異常が生じ、内皮機能障害や腸管バリアの破綻を介して心血管代謝疾患のリスクが高まると考えられています。
summary_en: This review synthesizes findings on how extreme temperature stress induces gut dysbiosis, characterized by a decrease in beneficial microbes and short-chain fatty acids. It discusses the mechanistic pathways linking these microbial alterations to impaired gut barrier integrity and increased risk of cardiometabolic diseases.
key_finding_ja: 極端な温度ストレスは腸内細菌叢のバランスを崩し、短鎖脂肪酸の減少や有害代謝物の増加を介して心血管代謝疾患のリスクを高める可能性がある。
why_it_matters_ja: 気候変動による健康被害が懸念される中、腸内細菌叢を標的としたプロバイオティクスや食事介入が、温度ストレスに伴う心血管代謝リスクを軽減する新たな手段となるかもしれない。

title: Targeting Mitochondrial Dysfunction in Microglia: A New Frontier for Treating Neurodegenerative Diseases.
abstract: Neurodegenerative diseases including Alzheimer's disease (AD), Parkinson's disease (PD), and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) pose an urgent global health challenge. Growing evidence establishes microglia-driven neuroinflammation as a key driver of disease onset and progression, with mitochondrial dysfunction emerging as an early trigger of microglial activation. This review comprehensively summarizes current progress on how mitochondrial alterations regulate microglial activation across AD, PD, and ALS. We identify conserved mechanisms including metabolic reprogramming, impaired mitophagy, and inflammatory signaling, though Aβ, α-synuclein, and TDP-43 engage these pathways through disease-specific molecular routes. Therapeutic strategies targeting microglial mitochondria, including cGAS-STING and NLRP3 inhibitors, TREM2 agonists, and mitochondrial transplantation, remain largely preclinical. Emerging targets such as OLFML3 and GPNMB require functional validation in microglia. Collectively, this review underscores that preserving microglial mitochondrial health represents a promising therapeutic frontier and identifies key priorities for translating these strategies toward clinical application.
authors: Chu M, Tan M, Gan X, Cui S, Shi L.
screening_reason: The review focuses directly on targeting mitochondrial dysfunction in microglia to modulate microglia-driven neuroinflammation in neurodegenerative diseases.
summary_ja: アルツハイマー病やパーキンソン病などの神経変性疾患において、ミクログリアが駆動する神経炎症が病態の進行に深く関与していることが明らかになりつつあります。本レビューでは、ミクログリアの活性化を誘発する初期の引き金としてのミトコンドリア機能障害に焦点を当て、その分子機構を包括的にまとめています。代謝再プログラミングやマイトファジーの障害、炎症シグナル伝達といった共通の機構を整理し、cGAS-STING阻害剤やTREM2作動薬などの治療戦略の現状を紹介しています。
summary_en: This review summarizes the role of microglial mitochondrial dysfunction as an early trigger for neuroinflammation in neurodegenerative diseases like Alzheimer's and Parkinson's. It highlights conserved mechanisms such as metabolic reprogramming and impaired mitophagy, while discussing preclinical therapeutic strategies targeting these pathways.
key_finding_ja: ミクログリアのミトコンドリア機能障害は神経炎症を誘発する重要な初期因子であり、代謝再プログラミングやマイトファジー障害などの共通機構を介して神経変性疾患の病態に関与している。
why_it_matters_ja: ミクログリアのミトコンドリアの健康維持を標的とした治療法は、神経変性疾患の新たな治療戦略となる可能性が期待されるが、臨床応用に向けてはさらなる機能検証が必要である。

title: SARS-CoV-2 Spike Peptides Trigger Nociceptive Responses Through Spinal TLR4 Pathways.
abstract: Background Pain is a common neurological manifestation of COVID-19, yet the mechanisms by which SARS-CoV-2 spike protein fragments contribute to nociceptive processing remain poorly understood. We investigated whether spike-derived peptides directly activate spinal neuroimmune pathways involved in pain signalling. Methods Male C57BL/6 mice received intrathecal administration of three synthetic SARS-CoV-2 spike-derived peptides (PSPD2001, PSPD2002 or PSPD2003) or saline. Mechanical nociception was assessed using the von Frey test. The involvement of spinal Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4), microglia and p38 MAPK/NF-κB signalling was investigated using pharmacological antagonists, TLR4 knockout mice, RT-qPCR, ELISA, immunofluorescence, CX3CR1 GFP/+ mice, human C20 microglial cells and molecular dynamics simulations. Results All spike-derived peptides induced mechanical nociception, with PSPD2003 producing the most pronounced response. PSPD2003 increased spinal TLR4 expression, elevated TNF-α and IL-6 levels and promoted activation of dorsal horn microglia, demonstrated by increased TMEM119- and CX3CR1-positive cells. These nociceptive and neuroinflammatory effects were abolished by pharmacological inhibition of TLR4, microglia, p38 MAPK and NF-κB signalling, as well as in TLR4 -/- mice, demonstrating that TLR4 signalling is essential for PSPD2003-induced pain. PSPD2003 also induced a hypertrophic phenotype in human microglial cells, while molecular dynamics simulations supported a stable interaction with the TLR4/MD-2 complex. Conclusions These findings identify a previously unrecognized neuroimmune mechanism whereby a SARS-CoV-2 spike-derived peptide triggers spinal nociception through TLR4-dependent microglial activation and downstream p38 MAPK/NF-κB signalling, highlighting the spinal TLR4-microglia axis as a potential therapeutic target for COVID-19-associated and post-viral pain. Significance statement This study provides the first evidence that SARS-CoV-2 spike-derived peptides directly activate a spinal TLR4-dependent neuroimmune pathway to induce nociception. By integrating behavioural, pharmacological, genetic, cellular and computational approaches, it identifies microglial activation and p38 MAPK/NF-κB signalling as key mechanisms linking viral peptides to pain, providing a mechanistic framework for COVID-19- and post-viral pain and supporting TLR4 as a potential therapeutic target.
authors: Silva BE, Cardoso RR, Rosário LMR, Prado JP, Dos Santos RS, Veras FP, de Souza M, Cilli EM, Olivier D, de Andrade Belo MA, Charlie-Silva I, Caixeta ES, Barchuk AR, Nunes-Silva A, Romero TRL, Galdino G.
screening_reason: Demonstrates a spinal neuroimmune pathway where microglial activation and TLR4 signaling mediate viral peptide-induced nociception.
summary_ja: COVID-19における神経障害としての痛みの発症メカニズムを解明するため、SARS-CoV-2スパイク由来ペプチドの脊髄における作用をマウスおよび細胞モデルで検証しました。スパイクペプチド（特にPSPD2003）を髄腔内投与すると、マウスで機械的疼痛様反応が誘発されることが判明しました。このノシセプション反応は、脊髄後角におけるミクログリア活性化、TLR4発現上昇、およびp38 MAPK/NF-κBシグナルの増強を伴っていました。遺伝子欠損マウスや阻害剤を用いた実験により、これらの変化がTLR4依存的であることが証明されました。
summary_en: Intrathecal administration of a SARS-CoV-2 spike-derived peptide induced mechanical nociception in mice by triggering spinal microglial activation. This effect was mediated by TLR4 signaling and downstream p38 MAPK/NF-κB pathways. Genetic knockout or pharmacological inhibition of TLR4 or microglia completely abolished the peptide-induced pain response.
key_finding_ja: SARS-CoV-2スパイク由来ペプチドが脊髄のTLR4-ミクログリア軸およびp38 MAPK/NF-κBシグナルを介して機械的疼痛を惹起することが明らかになった。
why_it_matters_ja: 脊髄のTLR4-ミクログリア経路は、COVID-19関連疼痛や感染後痛に対する新たな治療標的となる可能性を示唆しています。

title: Post-translational modifications in extracellular microvesicles from plasma of Rheumatoid Arthritis patients following anti-TNFα therapy.
abstract: Introduction Autoantibodies targeting post-translational modified proteins represent key immunological hallmarks of Rheumatoid Arthritis (RA). In a previous study we demonstrated the presence of citrullinated and carbamylated proteins in extracellular microvesicles (EMVs) from plasma of RA patients. Since the pivotal role of TNFα in sustaining inflammatory and oxidative processes that promote protein modification, in this study we investigated the patterns of these post-translational modifications in EMVs isolated from RA patients before and after anti-TNFα treatment. Methods Twelve consecutive RA patients, naïve to biological therapy, were enrolled and subjected to anti-TNFα therapy, which remained stable throughout 8 months of follow-up. EMVs, isolated from baseline (T0) and 8 months follow-up (T8) plasma of RA patients, were measured by Nanoparticle Tracking analysis or lysed and subjected to western blot analysis, using anti-citrulline or anti-Carbamyl Lysine antibodies. Anti-citrullinated and anti-carbamylated protein antibodies were also detected. Results Anti-TNFα treatment induced a significant reduction of concentration of EMVs isolated from plasma of RA patients after 8 months of anti-TNFα treatment (p Conclusion These findings suggest the role of EMVs, as well as of citrullinated and carbamylated protein levels, as potential indicators of RA activity.
authors: Recalchi S, Riitano G, Ucci F, Manganelli V, Garofalo T, Fratini F, Misasi R, Longo A, Alessandri C, Conti F, Capozzi A, Sorice M.
screening_reason: The study directly investigates specific post-translational modifications (citrullination and carbamylation) of proteins in extracellular microvesicles from rheumatoid arthritis patients.
summary_ja: 関節リウマチ（RA）患者の血漿由来細胞外マイクロベシクル（EMV）における、翻訳後修飾（シトルリン化およびカルバミル化）タンパク質の動態を調査した。生物学的製剤未治療のRA患者12名を対象に、抗TNFα療法を8ヶ月間行い、治療前後でのEMVの変化を解析した。その結果、治療後に血漿中EMVの濃度が有意に減少し、EMV内のシトルリン化およびカルバミル化タンパク質のレベルも低下した。これらの翻訳後修飾タンパク質の減少は、臨床的な疾患活動性の改善と並行して観察された。
summary_en: This clinical study investigated the patterns of post-translational modifications, specifically citrullination and carbamylation, in plasma extracellular microvesicles (EMVs) from rheumatoid arthritis (RA) patients undergoing anti-TNFα therapy. Following eight months of treatment, there was a significant reduction in both the concentration of EMVs and the levels of citrullinated and carbamylated proteins within them. These changes correlated with a decrease in clinical disease activity scores.
key_finding_ja: 抗TNFα療法により、関節リウマチ患者の血漿中細胞外マイクロベシクル（EMV）の濃度、およびEMV内のシトルリン化・カルバミル化タンパク質レベルが有意に減少することが明らかになった。
why_it_matters_ja: 細胞外マイクロベシクルにおける特定の翻訳後修飾タンパク質のレベルが、関節リウマチの疾患活動性や治療反応性を評価するための有用なバイオマーカーとなる可能性が示唆される。

title: Nanomedicine for epilepsy: Expanding beyond conventional drug targets.
abstract: Epilepsy remains a major neurological disorder characterized by unpredictable seizures and cumulative comorbidities that even endure with standard pharmacotherapy. Conventional antiepileptic drugs (AEDs) are constrained by two interrelated barriers: limited brain penetration due to the blood-brain barrier (BBB), which necessitates high systemic dosing and peripheral toxicity, and a narrow mechanistic focus on neuronal ion channels and synaptic receptors. This neuron-centric view overlooks non-neuronal drivers, such as neuroinflammation and BBB dysfunction, that sustain epileptogenesis and contribute to drug resistance in roughly one-third of patients. Nanomedicine addresses these limitations through a fundamentally different approach. Leveraging the unique advantages of nanocarriers, including facile synthesis, surface modification, and receptor-mediated BBB transcytosis, nanoparticles have evolved from passive delivery vehicles into intelligent, multifunctional therapeutic platforms that actively engage with disease biology. In this Perspective, we first delineate the inherent limitations of conventional AEDs in target selection. We then highlight how emerging nanomedicines are expanding the therapeutic target repertoire to include key non-neuronal nodes, with a focus on neuroinflammation and BBB repair. Finally, we offer a forward-looking perspective on two emerging frontiers: modulation of metabolic dysregulation and the microbiota-gut-brain axis, as well as the development of theranostic nanoplatforms that integrate real-time seizure monitoring with closed-loop intervention. Through this discussion, we aim to inspire a reorientation of nanomedicine strategies toward precision therapy for epilepsy.
authors: Sun Y, Liu W.
journal: Journal of controlled release : official journal of the Controlled Release Society
screening_reason: The paper discusses nanomedicine strategies targeting neuroinflammation and the microbiota-gut-brain axis for epilepsy therapy.
summary_ja: てんかん治療における従来の抗てんかん薬は、血液脳関門（BBB）の透過制限や、神経細胞のイオンチャネル等に限定された作用機序という課題を抱えている。これに対し、ナノテクノロジーを利用したナノ医薬品は、BBBを通過して病変部位に直接作用する多機能な治療プラットフォームとして期待されている。本展望では、神経炎症の抑制やBBBの修復といった非神経細胞標的へのアプローチに焦点を当てている。さらに、代謝異常の調節や腸脳相関の制御、リアルタイムのてんかん監視を統合したナノプラットフォームなどの新たなフロンティアについても議論している。
summary_en: Conventional antiepileptic drugs are limited by poor blood-brain barrier (BBB) penetration and a narrow focus on neuronal targets, overlooking non-neuronal drivers like neuroinflammation. Nanomedicine offers multifunctional platforms capable of crossing the BBB and targeting these non-neuronal pathways, including neuroinflammation and BBB dysfunction. This perspective highlights how emerging nanoparticles can expand the therapeutic repertoire to include metabolic regulation, the gut-brain axis, and theranostic systems.
key_finding_ja: ナノ医薬品を用いることで、従来の神経細胞中心の標的を超えて、神経炎症の抑制や血液脳関門の修復といった非神経細胞の病態生理学的プロセスを効果的に標的化できる可能性が示された。
why_it_matters_ja: 難治性てんかんの治療において、ナノテクノロジーを応用した多機能プラットフォームが、従来の薬剤耐性を克服する精密医療の実現に寄与することが期待される。

title: Microbiota-Neuroinflammation Crosstalk in Primary Brain Tumors: Focus on Glioblastoma.
abstract: Purpose Glioblastoma (GBM) is the most aggressive primary brain tumor in adults and remains difficult to treat because of diffuse invasion, immunosuppression, metabolic adaptability, and therapy resistance. This review evaluates how gut microbiota and microbiota-associated neuroinflammatory signaling may contribute to GBM biology and therapeutic response. Method We synthesized mechanistic, preclinical, translational, and emerging clinical evidence on microbiota-neuroinflammation interactions in GBM. The review focused on gut-brain axis pathways, microbial metabolites, blood-brain barrier (BBB) regulation, glial and myeloid immune activity, tumor-associated microbial signatures, microbial peptide-HLA presentation, and microbiome-informed biomarker or therapeutic strategies. Finding Current evidence suggests that microbiota-related signals may influence GBM through systemic immune modulation, short-chain fatty acids, tryptophan-derived metabolites, polyamines, BBB effects, and altered microglial and tumor-associated myeloid cell function. Polyamine metabolism may sustain myeloid-cell-mediated immunosuppression in the acidic GBM tumor microenvironment, whereas microglial GLUT5-dependent fructose metabolism may limit inflammatory antigen presentation and adaptive antitumor immunity. Sequencing-based studies have reported bacterial and fungal nucleic acid signatures in brain tumor specimens, but these findings require careful interpretation because of low biomass, contamination risk, and methodological variability. Preclinical models further indicate that microbiome modulation can alter inflammatory tone, tumor growth, immune-cell infiltration, and response to immune checkpoint blockade. Conclusion Microbiota-regulated neuroinflammation is a biologically plausible contributor to GBM progression, immune suppression, and treatment resistance. However, most evidence remains preclinical or early translational. Well-controlled, spatially resolved, multi-omic studies are required before microbiome-based biomarkers or interventions can be clinically implemented for patient stratification and future precision clinical neuro-oncology applications.
authors: AlRamadneh TN, S RJ, Nayak PP, Nanda A, Hasnaawei SA, Bhatt A, Chauhan AS, Singla S, Nourizadeh M.
screening_reason: Focuses on gut microbiota-neuroinflammation crosstalk and microbial metabolites in glioblastoma biology.
summary_ja: 膠芽腫（GBM）の病態における腸内細菌叢と神経炎症シグナルの相互作用に関する知見を概括したレビューである。短鎖脂肪酸やポリアミンなどの微生物由来代謝物が、ミクログリアや腫瘍関連骨髄系細胞の機能を変化させ、免疫抑制性微小環境に寄与する可能性が示されている。また、脳腫瘍サンプル中の微生物核酸シグネチャーの報告はあるものの、低バイオマスや汚染リスクに注意が必要であると指摘されている。
summary_en: This review examines the interactions between gut microbiota and neuroinflammatory signaling in glioblastoma progression and therapeutic resistance. Microbial metabolites and immune pathways influence microglial behavior, blood-brain barrier integrity, and the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. While microbiome modulation shows potential in preclinical studies, rigorous multi-omic research is needed prior to clinical implementation.
key_finding_ja: 腸内細菌叢に関連するシグナルは、神経炎症や腫瘍関連免疫細胞の機能を介して膠芽腫の進行や治療抵抗性に影響を与える可能性がある。
why_it_matters_ja: 膠芽腫における免疫抑制機序の解明や、将来的な微生物叢に着目した個別化医療アプローチの開発につながる期待がある。

title: In-Vitro Evaluation of HIV/SARS-CoV-2 Co-Infection Mediated Proteomic Changes in Astrocytes and Pericytes Reveals Altered Signaling Pathways Associated With Neurodegenerative Disorders.
abstract: Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) survivors frequently experience a wide range of symptoms known as post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 (PASC) or long COVID. Importantly, complications arising from microvascular dysfunction, blood-brain barrier (BBB) disruption, and chronic neuroinflammation have been implicated in driving PASC within the central nervous system (CNS), known as neuro-PASC. Notably, people with HIV (PWH), who suffer from chronic neuroinflammation, BBB impairment, and glial cell dysfunction, collectively known as neuro-HIV, are generally at higher risk of neuro-PASC. The overlap between neuro-PASC and neuro-HIV raises concerns that HIV and SARS-CoV-2 co-infection may exacerbate neurological dysfunctions among PWH. In this study, using an in-vitro cell culture model, we examine the effects of HIV and SARS-CoV-2 mono- and co-infection in microglia, astrocytes, and pericytes. Our results demonstrated that majority of brain cell types support SARS-CoV-2 replication, in the presence and absence of HIV infection. Furthermore, in both mono- and co-infected cells, there were varying degree of up- and downregulation of SARS-CoV-2 host cell entry factors, such as ACE2, TMPRSS2, NRP1, and TRIM28, and inflammatory cytokines including IL-6, TNF-α, and IL-1β. Moreover, conditioned media collected from HIV, SARS-CoV-2, and HIV/SARS-CoV-2 co-infected astrocytes and pericytes were shown to be neurotoxic. Additionally, proteomic analysis has revealed a unique set of proteins significantly up/down regulated in HIV/SARS-CoV-2 co-infected astrocytes and pericytes. The gene set enrichment analysis of these proteins indicates dysregulation of lipid, energy, and immune metabolism pathways linked to neurodegenerative disorders like Alzheimer's, Parkinson's, Huntington's disease, and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis. These in-vitro findings indicate that astrocytes and pericytes from HIV/SARS-CoV-2 co-infection exhibit altered protein expression profiles, implicating dysregulated signaling pathways associated with neurodegenerative dysfunction.
authors: Acharya A, Thurman M, Sutar D, Olasunkanmi OI, Malik JR, Dyavar SR, Végvári Á, Byrareddy SN.
screening_reason: Examines glial neuroinflammation, cytokine expression, and neuroimmune signaling in HIV and SARS-CoV-2 CNS co-infection.
summary_ja: HIVおよびSARS-CoV-2の単独感染および共感染がミクログリア、アストロサイト、ペリサイトに与える影響をin vitroモデルで検証した。脳細胞の多くは感染の有無に関わらずウイルス複製を支持し、エントリー因子や炎症性サイトカインの発現変化が確認された。感染したアストロサイトおよびペリサイトからの条件培地は神経毒性を示した。プロテオミクス解析では、脂質・エネルギー・免疫代謝経路の異常が示され、神経変性疾患に関連するシグナル伝達の変化が明らかになった。
summary_en: This in vitro study investigated the impact of HIV and SARS-CoV-2 mono- and co-infection on microglia, astrocytes, and pericytes. Both mono- and co-infections altered the expression of host entry factors and inflammatory cytokines, and conditioned media from infected astrocytes and pericytes exhibited neurotoxicity. Proteomic analysis revealed significant dysregulation of lipid, energy, and immune metabolic pathways associated with neurodegenerative disorders.
key_finding_ja: HIVとSARS-CoV-2の共感染はアストロサイトやペリサイトのタンパク質発現を変化させ、神経変性疾患に関連するシグナル伝達経路の障害を引き起こす。
why_it_matters_ja: 本研究はin vitroモデルに基づくものであり、ヒト体内におけるHIVとSARS-CoV-2の共感染が神経変性やNeuro-PASCの発症リスクを高める可能性を示唆している。

title: Gut microbiota-derived trimethylamine N-oxide (TMAO) and its association with neuroinflammation in migraine.
abstract: Background and objectives Migraine is a common primary headache disorder associated with neuroinflammation, with evidence implicating gut microbiota and metabolites in neurological mechanisms pathways. Since trimethylamine-N-oxide (TMAO), derived from dietary precursors by gut microbial metabolism, is associated with cardiovascular and neurodegenerative conditions, and its role in migraines is unclear, we aimed to evaluate whether serum TMAO level and related metabolites in migraine patients can be biomarkers. Methods A total of 106 participants were enrolled, consisting of healthy controls (n=46; mean age ± SD=39±8 yr old) and migraine patients (n=60). The migraine cohort was divided into migraine with aura (n=18; mean age±SD=33±11 yr old) and migraine without aura (n=42; mean age±SD=37±10 yr old), according to the International Classification of Headache Disorders, 3rd edition (ICHD-3). Blood samples were centrifuged, stored at -80°C, and analysed for TMAO, carnitine, betaine, and choline levels using liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS). Results There were no significant differences between the groups for age, smoking, or body mass index (BMI). Serum TMAO levels were significantly higher in patients with migraine with aura [2.75 (1.98-3.91) ng/mL] and migraine without aura [2.85 (2.08-5.53) ng/mL] compared to controls [1.40 (1.00-3.01) ng/mL] (P<0.001). Serum choline, betaine, and carnitine levels were significantly higher in the migraine groups (all P < 0.01). Interpretation and conclusions These findings indicate elevated TMAO levels in patients with migraine, suggesting a possible involvement of TMAO in migraine-associated neuroinflammatory processes. Targeted studies and cohort-based investigations are needed to clarify its role in migraine and evaluate its potential as a biomarker.
authors: Atıcı Y, Eruyar E, Ökten Z, Serdar CC, Serdar MA, Yücel D.
journal: The Indian journal of medical research
screening_reason: Investigates gut microbiota-derived trimethylamine N-oxide (TMAO) and its association with neuroinflammatory processes in migraine.
summary_ja: 本臨床研究では、偏頭痛患者60名（有前兆18名、無前兆42名）と健常対照者46名を対象に、腸内細菌由来代謝物であるトリメチルアミン-N-オキシド（TMAO）および関連代謝物の血清濃度を測定した。解析の結果、偏頭痛患者群では有前兆・無前兆にかかわらず、対照群と比較して血清TMAO、コリン、ベタイン、カルニチン濃度が有意に高値であった。これらの結果は、TMAOが偏頭痛に伴う神経炎症プロセスに関与している可能性を示唆している。著者らは、バイオマーカーとしての有用性や詳細な役割の解明に向けたさらなる検証が必要であると結論付けている。
summary_en: This clinical study evaluated serum levels of gut microbiota-derived trimethylamine N-oxide (TMAO) and related metabolites in 60 migraine patients and 46 healthy controls. Serum TMAO, choline, betaine, and carnitine levels were significantly elevated in migraine patients both with and without aura compared to controls. These findings suggest that TMAO may be involved in migraine-associated neuroinflammatory processes and could serve as a potential biomarker.
key_finding_ja: 偏頭痛患者の血清中において、腸内細菌由来代謝物TMAOおよびその関連前駆体の濃度が健常対照者と比較して有意に高値であった。
why_it_matters_ja: 偏頭痛におけるTMAOの関与が確認されれば、診断バイオマーカーとしての活用や腸内細菌代謝を標的とした新たな治療法開発につながる可能性がある。

title: Gut Microbiome and ADHD: A Narrative Review of Clinical Evidence and Practice Implications.
abstract: Objective This narrative review evaluates the current evidence on the efficacy of probiotic interventions for Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) symptoms in both medicated and drug-naïve paediatric and adult populations and assesses the implications for clinical dietetic practice. Design A narrative review synthesizing randomized controlled trials and observational microbiome studies in paediatric and adult populations, specifically distinguishing between probiotic monotherapy and adjunctive protocols. Results Observational data confirm gut microbiome alterations in ADHD populations, although specific bacterial signatures vary across studies. Evidence from treatment trials demonstrates that the efficacy of probiotics as monotherapy for core ADHD symptoms remains inconclusive. However, specific adjunctive trials combining probiotics with conventional medication have reported preliminary positive findings on symptom reduction, though results remain heterogeneous. Adult evidence is sparse but indicates potential benefits for emotional dysregulation in specific contexts. Conclusions This review concludes that current data do not support universal probiotic supplementation or routine clinical recommendation. However, when families inquire about complementary approaches, the existing literature enables evidence informed guidance within a shared decision-making framework that acknowledges the preliminary nature of current findings and sets realistic expectations.
authors: Sadowska K, Hart K.
journal: Journal of human nutrition and dietetics : the official journal of the British Dietetic Association
screening_reason: This review evaluates the clinical evidence regarding gut microbiome alterations and probiotic interventions in ADHD.
summary_ja: 本ナラティブレビューは、ADHD患者における腸内細菌叢の変化と、ADHD症状に対するプロバイオティクス介入の有効性に関する臨床エビデンスを評価した。観察研究ではADHD患者における腸内細菌叢の変化が確認されているものの、プロバイオティクス単独療法による中核症状への効果は依然として結論が出ていない。一方で、通常の治療薬とプロバイオティクスを組み合わせた併用療法では一部で予備的な好結果が報告されており、現時点では一律の推奨ではなく、個別の意思決定に基づく指導が推奨される。
summary_en: This narrative review evaluates the clinical evidence regarding gut microbiome alterations and the efficacy of probiotic interventions for ADHD symptoms. While observational studies confirm gut microbiota changes in individuals with ADHD, evidence for probiotics as a monotherapy remains inconclusive. However, some adjunctive trials combining probiotics with conventional medication show preliminary positive results, supporting evidence-informed guidance rather than routine clinical recommendation.
key_finding_ja: ADHDに対するプロバイオティクス単独療法の効果は不十分であるが、通常の治療薬との併用療法においては予備的な改善効果が示されている。
why_it_matters_ja: ADHD患者やその家族が補完代替療法を希望する際、現在の科学的根拠に基づいた現実的な期待値設定と意思決定を支援するための臨床的指針となる。

title: Exploring community-level gut health amidst COVID-19 pandemic: a proposed application of longitudinal wastewater surveillance.
abstract: Wastewater-based epidemiology (WBE) offers a unique, scalable method to monitor disease burden at a community level by capturing all individuals within a sewershed. While emerging evidence suggests that SARS-CoV-2 may influence the human gut microbiota, which is essential for health and disease outcomes, most microbiome studies remain limited to the individual scale. Given wastewater's sensitivity to fluctuations in human fecal composition, we propose leveraging WBE as a cost-effective tool to characterize longitudinal microbial shifts in community-level gut microbiota throughout the COVID-19 pandemic. In this exploratory study, we analyze wastewater from two central Ohio, USA, cities, Columbus and Newark, which differ in socioeconomic and demographic characteristics. Monthly influent samples (n = 69) were collected from August 2020 through June 2022. Clinical COVID-19 cases were collected from within each sewershed, and SARS-CoV-2 gene concentrations were quantified from wastewater samples. 16S rRNA gene sequencing was conducted to characterize human-gut-associated bacterial communities. We report that wastewater influent exhibits distinct genus-level bacterial signatures reflective of each catchment population. Significant temporal changes in bacterial structure and diversity were observed across both cities, indicating community gut health shifts throughout the pandemic. Several taxa, including but not limited to Collinsella, Megasphaera, and Actinobacteriota, showed notable relative abundance fluctuations that may be linked to infection and warrant further investigation as potential microbial biomarkers. This study demonstrates that urban population-level gut microbiome patterns can be robustly characterized through wastewater influent. Most notably, this 23-month study represents the first effort to examine community gut microbiota structural changes across two cities during the COVID-19 pandemic. Our findings highlight sewage as a population-level proxy for public health status and disease burden while offering a novel framework for integrating microbiome science into WBE. This study underscores the potential of wastewater surveillance to advance global infectious disease preparedness and population-scale microbiome research.
authors: Lancaster E, Ai Y, Lee J.
journal: Environmental science and pollution research international
screening_reason: The study utilizes wastewater surveillance to characterize longitudinal shifts in the community-level human gut microbiome.
summary_ja: 本探索的研究は、下水疫学（WBE）を利用して、COVID-19パンデミック下におけるオハイオ州の2都市のコミュニティレベルでの腸内細菌叢の経時的変化を追跡した。23ヶ月間にわたる月ごとの下水流入水の分析により、各都市に固有の細菌シグネチャーと、細菌叢の構造および多様性における有意な経時的変化が明らかになった。CollinsellaやMegasphaeraなどの特定の分類群の相対存在量に顕著な変動が見られ、これらは感染状況と関連している可能性が示唆された。
summary_en: This exploratory study utilized wastewater-based epidemiology to monitor longitudinal shifts in community-level gut microbiota across two Ohio cities during the COVID-19 pandemic. Analysis of monthly influent samples over 23 months revealed distinct, city-specific bacterial signatures and significant temporal changes in microbial structure and diversity. Fluctuations in specific taxa, such as Collinsella and Megasphaera, were observed, suggesting potential links to infection rates.
key_finding_ja: 下水流入水の分析を通じて、パンデミック期における都市コミュニティレベルの腸内細菌叢の構造および多様性の経時的変化を捉えることに成功した。
why_it_matters_ja: 個別サンプリングに頼らずに集団規模の腸内環境や健康状態を監視する安価な手法として、下水監視が感染症対策や公衆衛生研究に貢献する可能性がある。

title: Barbaloin Attenuates Cisplatin-Induced Hippocampal Neurotoxicity by Suppressing Oxidative Stress, Neuroinflammation, and Apoptosis: In Vivo and In Silico Evidence.
abstract: The neurotoxicity of cisplatin (CIS) in the hippocampal leads to cognitive effects caused by oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, apoptosis, and dysfunction of neurotransmitters. The major bioactive phytonutrient in Aloe vera is barbaloin (BLN), which has been shown to have antioxidant and anti-inflammatory effects, but its neuroprotective ability against CIS-induced neurotoxicity has not been investigated. To assess the neuroprotective action of BLN in CIS-induced hippocampal neurotoxicity in rats and to understand the molecular interactions between BLN and major neuroinflammatory and apoptotic proteins. A total of 24 male Wistar rats were split into 4 groups (n = 6): control, CIS (5 mg/kg), CIS + BLN 25 mg/kg, and CIS + BLN 50 mg/kg over 21 days. Cognitive ability (Morris water maze), oxidative stress indicators (MDA, GSH, SOD, CAT), neuroinflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IL-1β, IL-6, NF-κB, TGF-β1), caspase-3, neurotransmitters, and hippocampal histopathology were measured. Molecular docking and 100-ns molecular dynamics simulations (MDS) with MM-GBSA analysis were done with TNF-α, TGF-β1, NF-κBp65, and caspase-3. BLN significantly reduced cognitive impairment, oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, and apoptosis, and restored neurotransmitter homeostasis and hippocampal cytoarchitecture (all p bind = -56.07 kcal/mol for TGF-β1). BLN exhibits considerable neuroprotective properties against CIS-induced neurotoxicity in the hippocampus, suggesting its potential as a natural dietary phytonutrient supplement to ameliorate chemotherapy-induced cognitive impairment.
authors: Syed RU, Akasha R, Elafandy NM, Abobaker SH, Al-Shammari AN, Altwalah LA, Aldafeeri RMM, Alfaki AIMA, Khan MSA, Ahmed AA.
journal: Journal of biochemical and molecular toxicology
screening_reason: The study directly measures and demonstrates the suppression of neuroinflammatory cytokines and neurotoxicity in the hippocampus by barbaloin.
summary_ja: 本研究は、抗がん剤シスプラチン（CIS）によって誘導される海馬の神経毒性に対し、アロエベラに含まれるバルバロイン（BLN）の保護効果をラットモデルおよびイン・シリコ解析で検証した。CISを投与したラットにおいて、BLNの投与は認知機能障害、酸化ストレス、神経炎症、アポトーシスを有意に抑制した。さらに、BLNは海馬の組織構造と神経伝達物質の恒常性を回復させた。分子ドッキングおよび分子動力学シミュレーションにおいても、BLNはTNF-αやTGF-β1などの主要な炎症・アポトーシス関連タンパク質と強い結合親和性を示した。
summary_en: This study investigated the protective effects of barbaloin (BLN) against cisplatin-induced hippocampal neurotoxicity using rat models and in silico simulations. BLN administration significantly ameliorated cognitive impairment, oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, and apoptosis in cisplatin-treated rats while restoring neurotransmitter levels. Computational docking and molecular dynamics simulations confirmed strong binding interactions between BLN and key neuroinflammatory and apoptotic proteins.
key_finding_ja: バルバロインは酸化ストレス、神経炎症、アポトーシスを抑制することにより、シスプラチン誘発性の海馬神経毒性および認知機能障害を軽減した。
why_it_matters_ja: 化学療法に伴う認知機能障害（ケモブレイン）を軽減するサプリメントや補助療法としてバルバロインの有効性が示唆されるが、臨床応用にはヒトでの安全性と有効性の検証が必要である。

title: Age-Associated B Cells: Origins, Regulation, and Tissue-Specific Pathogenic Contributions in Autoimmune, Metabolic, and Neurological Diseases.
abstract: Age-associated B cells (ABCs) are a distinct B cell population characterized by coexpression of T-bet and CD11c. First described in aged female mice and autoimmune-prone strains, ABCs are now recognized to be associated with multiple human autoimmune diseases, including systemic lupus erythematosus, rheumatoid arthritis, and multiple sclerosis, where their frequency correlates with disease activity. Their differentiation requires toll-like receptor (TLR) signaling, IFN-γ, IL-21, BCR engagement, with ZEB2 emerging as the nonredundant transcriptional master regulator of ABC identity. Here we review requirements for ABC differentiation, their defining phenotypic and functional features, and their tissue-specific distribution and pathogenic contributions in diverse inflammatory settings. A central theme is that ABCs are tissue-homing cells whose contribution extends beyond blood and lymphoid organs. In kidney, inflamed synovium, salivary glands, and adipose tissue, ABCs drive pathology through locally differentiated autoantibody-secreting cells, stromal activation, antigen presentation, and cytokine production. We further discuss roles for ABCs in neurological diseases, including their enrichment in the cerebrospinal fluid in multiple sclerosis (MS) and their contribution to neuroinflammation in Alzheimer's disease, and highlight the EBV-ABC axis as a mechanism linking viral infection to autoimmunity. In summary, ABCs are multi-functional, tissue-adaptable pathogenic effectors whose contributions to human disease extend beyond classical autoimmunity into metabolic dysfunction and neurodegeneration.
authors: Rubtsova K.
screening_reason: The review focuses on age-associated B cells and their contribution to neuroinflammation and neuroimmune interactions in CNS diseases.
summary_ja: 本総説は、T-betおよびCD11cを共発現する加齢関連B細胞（ABC）の分化機構と各種疾患での病理学的役割をまとめている。ABCの分化にはTLRシグナルやサイトカイン刺激、マスター転写因子ZEB2が必須であり、全身性エリテマトーデスや多発性硬化症などの自己免疫疾患で頻度が増加する。ABCは血中だけでなく腎臓、滑膜、中枢神経系などの組織へ浸潤し、自己抗体産生やサイトカイン放出を通じて局所炎症を引き起こす。さらに、多発性硬化症の髄液中での集積やアルツハイマー病における神経炎症への寄与についても論じられている。
summary_en: This review summarizes the origins, differentiation, and tissue-specific pathogenic roles of age-associated B cells (ABCs) expressing T-bet and CD11c.
